title: OSC 52: programs cannot reach the clipboard — xterm.js drops the sequence
description:
xterm.js registers OSC handlers for 0,1,2,4,8,10,11,12,104,110,111,112 and silently discards everything else, so OSC 52 never arrives. Any program that copies on the user's behalf therefore reaches nothing, with no error: Claude Code (verified in binary 2.1.217 — ']52;c;' with a tmux branch, plus pbcopy/xclip/xsel/wl-copy fallbacks), tmux, vim with clipboard=unnamed, and everything over SSH where OSC 52 is the only route to a local clipboard at all. This is a silent regression against every terminal the user already runs.

Fix through parser.registerOscHandler(52, ...) — the same mechanism already carrying OSC 7 in frontend/src/renderers/xterm.ts:188. registerOscHandler accepts arbitrary identifiers, so no engine patch is needed.

Do NOT copy Tabby's approach (tabby-terminal/src/middleware/oscProcessing.ts): it re-parses the byte stream ahead of the engine, which duplicates VT parsing that AD-6 assigns to the VT frontend, and at line 57 it buffers the remainder without bound or timeout when no terminator arrives — a stream carrying an unterminated sequence stalls output while accumulating memory. Registering on the engine's parser inherits chunk reassembly and both terminator forms for free; the engine also already caps an OSC payload at 1e7 chars.

Write only. The read form (]52;c;?) must have no code path, so a remote host on an SSH session cannot exfiltrate the clipboard. iTerm2, kitty and wezterm take the same stance; Tabby arrives there implicitly by honouring only targets 'c' and empty.
acceptance_criteria: printf '\033]52;c;<base64>\007' places the decoded text on the system clipboard; selecting text inside a Claude Code session running in nocx reaches the clipboard; the read form is ignored entirely.
close_reason: OSC 52 arrives through parser.registerOscHandler(52,...) beside the existing OSC 7 handler — no byte-stream middleware, so no repeat of Tabby's unbounded buffer. Writes are denied by default with a Warp-style banner carrying the remedy (allow / don't show again / dismiss); the read form has no code path at all. Decoder rejects the read form, non-clipboard targets, malformed base64, zero-byte payloads, and oversized ones before decoding. Verified by hand: printf of an OSC 52 sequence leaves the clipboard untouched after dismissing the banner. Note a local program can still reach the clipboard via pbcopy — no terminal gates that, Warp included; this protects what has no second door, i.e. content over SSH.

title: [bug] Glyph corruption on resize and after closing a tab
description:
Two reproductions of what is almost certainly one renderer defect, both reported with screenshots by the owner.
(a) Resize the window: existing glyphs turn into mangled overlapping shapes.
(b) Close the last tab, land on the neighbour, type: red garbage appears instead of characters.
25de485 made the ResizeObserver call refreshAtlas() instead of a bare clearTextureAtlas(), which was supposed to cover (a); it is evidently not enough, or the repaint happens before the new grid is in place. Note the tab-activation path also calls refreshAtlas(), which is the (b) path.
An earlier e2e attempt at this failed to discriminate because it nudged the pane by 1px on purpose to avoid a reflow — the real trigger changes the grid. A test driving page.setViewportSize() to a genuinely different cols/rows should reproduce it (see nocx-bq7).
acceptance_criteria: A real window resize and a close-tab-then-type both leave the screen rendering correctly, and an e2e test fails without the fix.
notes:
e2e pixel-test investigation (worker task_42e778c10d9f), 2026-07-22:

Engines tried:
- Playwright Chromium (headless): WebGL IS active (confirmed via canvas webgl2 context probe of the xterm renderer canvas). Pixel tests pass identically with the fix reverted — the corruption does NOT reproduce in headless Chromium. This was already known from a prior attempt.
- Playwright WebKit (headless): WebGL IS active (same confirmation method). Pixel tests ALSO pass identically with the fix reverted — the corruption does NOT reproduce in headless WebKit either.

Conclusion: no automated guard is achievable from this harness. The glyph corruption (mangled overlapping glyphs on resize, red garbage after close-tab-and-type) is specific to the real macOS WKWebView rendering context inside the Wails app. Neither Playwright engine reproduces it.

xterm.ts change (IN PLACE and UNVERIFIED against visible symptom as of handoff):
refreshAtlas() formerly called clearTextureAtlas() then term.refresh(0, rows-1). It now calls only term.refresh(0, rows-1). Rationale: clearing the texture atlas before repainting races with atlas repopulation in _updateModel. The resize path (safeFit to fit to handleResize) already refreshes the char atlas via _refreshCharAtlas(). The tab-activation path needs only a viewport refresh.

Steps 4-5 (real-app verification) are PENDING a human check:
- Resize the real WKWebView window: check for mangled overlapping glyphs
- Close a tab and type on the survivor: check for red garbage
- One tab, type: check prompt stays intact (nocx-d1f regression)

Cleanup done:
- e2e/screenshots/ deleted (leftover PNGs from prior investigation)
- /e2e/screenshots/ added to .gitignore
- No pixel test shipped (would pass in both states = false guard)

If the fix is wrong: the refreshAtlas change is the only change. To revert, restore clearTextureAtlas() calls before term.refresh().
close_reason:
Verified by the repo owner in the real WKWebView app, which is the only place this reproduces: resize no longer mangles glyphs, close-tab-then-type shows no red garbage, and nocx-d1f has not regressed (one tab, click, type renders correctly) — that last check mattered because the fix removes the clearTextureAtlas() call that 25de485 had paired with a refresh.

Fix: refreshAtlas() in frontend/src/renderers/xterm.ts now only calls term.refresh(0, rows-1); the clearTextureAtlas() call is gone, because clearing before repainting races with atlas repopulation in _updateModel while the resize path already refreshes the char atlas via _refreshCharAtlas().

No automated guard ships, deliberately. Both Playwright engines were tried with the fix reverted — Chromium and WebKit, WebGL confirmed active in each — and NEITHER reproduces the corruption. A test that passes in both states is a false guard, so none was written; the finding is recorded in the notes instead. Our e2e harness is structurally blind to this class of bug.

title: Playwright webServer leaves wails dev and its vite watcher running
description: Driving 'wails dev' from Playwright's webServer does not tear down cleanly, so a run hangs for minutes after the last test and would burn a CI job's timeout. Measured: the frontend dev watcher runs in its OWN process group (vite PGID 33952, parent 'npm run dev' reparented to PPID 1) while Playwright's group is separate (33771), so neither Playwright's group kill nor a 'trap kill 0' in the webServer command can reach it. The orphan inherits the run's stdio, so with stdout/stderr piped the stream never reaches EOF; one observed run only exited after vite happened to crash with EPIPE, 3.4 minutes for 7 seconds of tests. Runs also leave 'wails dev' itself alive afterwards. Options: a globalTeardown that reaps by port and by the project-scoped vite path, or a globalSetup that starts the server under setsid and kills the whole tree.
acceptance_criteria: A full e2e run exits within seconds of the last test and leaves no wails dev, app or vite process behind.
close_reason: Fixed by gracefulShutdown: {signal: 'SIGTERM'} in playwright.config.ts. Root cause confirmed in the wails v2.13.0 source: the CLI starts the frontend watcher with Setpgid (dev_other.go:15) and reaps it from a SIGTERM handler via syscall.Kill(-pgid) (dev_other.go:32, dev.go:90/114). Playwright's default is to SIGKILL the group, so that handler never ran. Verified from a clean process table: 4 passed in 15.7s, 16.4s wall clock (was 3m26s for fewer tests), and no wails dev, app or vite process left behind.

title: e2e regression test for nocx-d1f: click-to-focus and atlas repaint
description: nocx-d1f was fixed in 25de485 (ResizeObserver refreshAtlas) and 2c02a46 (#panes --wails-draggable: no-drag) but no test guards either half, so both can silently regress. The bug class is invisible to jsdom: no layout, no GPU, no focus. Add an e2e spec on the existing Playwright harness at :34115 covering (a) a click on the pane hands focus to the terminal and typed characters reach it, (b) the pane render is stable across the deferred ResizeObserver run rather than being left on a cleared atlas.
acceptance_criteria: A spec in e2e/ passes against the current tree and fails when the 25de485 fix is reverted.
notes:
Landed: e2e/click-focus.spec.ts (click -> focus -> keystroke -> PTY -> tab title round trip), plus a self-starting webServer in playwright.config.ts.
Deliberately NOT landed: an e2e guard for the atlas half. An attempt (1px sub-cell nudge to fire the ResizeObserver without reflowing the grid, then a forced row repaint, compared against a tab-switch refreshAtlas as ground truth) passed identically with 25de485 reverted — verified the revert really reached the browser by curling the served module (clearTextureAtlas twice, no refreshAtlas). xterm re-rasterizes glyphs lazily on the next draw, so a cleared atlas repaints correctly from outside; the original corruption needed a tighter race than a test can stage. A vacuous test is worse than none, so it was deleted.
Still open as a follow-up: guard the invariant itself (an atlas clear is always followed by a refresh) at unit level, driving a stubbed ResizeObserver in the vitest suite — jsdom has no WebGL, but term.refresh() is still observable.
close_reason: Delivered as e2e/click-focus.spec.ts, which locks the path the bug travelled: click -> focus -> keystroke -> PTY -> response (focus target is .nocx-editor-input post-nocx-4ff). The atlas-repaint half was deliberately NOT kept: the candidate test passed just as happily with fix 25de485 reverted, so it guarded nothing and was deleted; --wails-draggable is likewise unprovable in Chromium (inert custom property, only native WKWebView reads it). Reasoning is recorded in the spec header, e2e/click-focus.spec.ts:3-21.

title: Terminal leaked its launcher's agent session into every shell
description: nocx handed the whole parent environment to every PTY (cmd.Env = os.Environ()), so when it is started from inside a coding agent — which is how it gets developed — each shell inherited that agent's session markers. A 'claude' run in a nocx tab saw CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION and silently turned transcript saving off; the user hit this for real. The principle is general: a terminal hands out shells and must not hand out its launcher's identity with them. Fixed by scrubbing a precise list of session markers (not a CLAUDE* wildcard — stripping something like an API key would break the very tool being fixed). Related and still open: nocx does not start a LOGIN shell, so the environment is whatever nocx inherited rather than what the user's profile defines. Terminal.app runs the first shell with -l. Worth a separate look.
acceptance_criteria: A shell opened in nocx carries no launcher session markers; credentials and ordinary variables survive.
close_reason: Closed

title: Tier A shell hooks: make the shell emit OSC 133 command markers
description:
nocx-5mn.1 verified we can RECEIVE OSC 133 (ADR-0001: xterm.js returned A, B, C, D;0 and D;127 with exit codes). Nothing yet makes a shell SEND them, so every consumer of command boundaries is starved. AD-5 Tier A is exactly this: shell hooks with zero remote install, working locally and over SSH. Ship the zsh/bash hooks and inject them so a user gets this without configuring anything. Emit A at prompt start, B at prompt end, C when output starts, and D with the exit code when the command finishes.

SCOPE CORRECTION (2026-07-22): the old description claimed this unlocks the activity indicator 'driven by real command completion instead of byte heuristics (nocx-5mf)'. That is dead. nocx-5mf shipped in 2d990ee via the title-status layer (frontend/src/agent-status.ts + Tab.updateAgentStatus) and its close reason records the OSC 133 dependency as a modelling error: the two are complementary, since OSC 133 marks SHELL command boundaries and cannot see inside one long-running agent command. Do not cite nocx-5mf as justification here again — it cost a session of picking already-done work.

What genuinely remains behind these markers, and nothing else: command blocks, success/failure colouring from the D exit code, and 'a background command finished' as an explicit event rather than a byte heuristic.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a shell in nocx produces OSC 133 A/B/C/D at the right boundaries, D carries the exit code, and the frontend receives them through the registered handler.
notes: SCOPE ADDITION (2026-07-23, ADR-0004): the injected hooks must ALSO install a marker-only, visually empty prompt in enhanced mode (empty PROMPT/PS1 carrying only the OSC markers), saving and restoring the user's original prompt when integration is off or nocx exits. This is what lets the DOM input editor (nocx-4ff) own composition without a duplicate shell prompt. Raw fallback stays mandatory: if hooks/markers are absent, behave as a conventional terminal.

title: Activity indicator is always on for full-screen TUIs
description: Tabs running Claude Code or Hermes show the activity indicator permanently: those TUIs animate spinners and elapsed-time counters, so bytes never stop arriving, and any output currently counts as activity. The indicator answers 'did bytes arrive' when the user needs 'did something happen worth my attention'. Note Tabby has the identical flaw — baseTerminalTab.component.ts subscribes binaryOutput$ straight to displayActivity() — so copying it faithfully is what produced this; do not look there for the fix. Proposed rule: in the normal screen buffer any output is activity, as today; in the ALTERNATE screen buffer repaints are ignored, because a full-screen TUI redrawing itself is not news — but a bell (BEL) always counts, since that is a program explicitly asking for attention. xterm.js exposes buffer.active.type and onBell. Keep AD-6 intact: the renderer reports the facts (which buffer is active, a bell fired), the tab decides the policy — tabs.ts must not sniff bytes.
design:
How Warp does it: it does not guess from output — the SHELL tells it, via OSC 133 semantic prompt markers. A = prompt start, B = prompt end / input start, C = command output start, D;<exit> = command finished with its exit code. Ghostty, iTerm2, Kitty and WezTerm use the same substrate. 'A command finished in a background tab' is therefore an explicit event, not a heuristic, and it carries success or failure with it.

We already proved we can receive this. ADR-0001 chose xterm.js precisely because registering parser.registerOscHandler returned all five OSC 133 markers — A, B, C, D;0 and D;127 — exit codes included, where ghostty-web exposed no OSC handler registration at all. AD-5 already names OSC 133 as the Tier A substrate and epic nocx-5mn owns the shell hooks.

So the indicator should be driven by OSC 133 D, not by counting bytes: light it when a command finishes in a background tab, and it can then say more than 'something happened' — a failed command (D;non-zero) deserves a different colour from a successful one, which is what Warp shows.

Scope boundary worth stating: OSC 133 marks SHELL command boundaries. It fires when a long build ends, and when claude itself exits — but it says nothing while claude is running and wants attention mid-session, because that is inside one shell command. That case needs the program to signal: a bell, or OSC 9. Claude Code currently emits neither (see anthropics/claude-code issues #22528 and #32635, both open requests for OSC 133 support). Keep the bell rule for it and do not pretend the byte heuristic can cover it.

This makes nocx-5mf depend on the Tier A shell hooks in nocx-5mn rather than on more heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: A tab running a spinner TUI in the alternate screen stops showing a permanent activity indicator; a bell inside that TUI still lights it; ordinary shell output in the normal buffer still lights it.
notes:
How Orca does the spinning tab indicator (/Users/shady/Documents/repos/orca, src/shared/terminal-title-status.ts): detectAgentStatusFromTitle(title) classifies the TERMINAL TITLE into three states — 'working', 'idle', 'permission' — not two. Markers: Claude Code prefixes the title with ✳ when idle and with a braille spinner while working; Gemini CLI has its own symbols for all three; Pi/OMP use synthetic labels; a braille spinner anywhere in the title means working. Cursor's bare native title is explicitly excluded as carrying no status.

We can do this today with what we already have: renderer.onTitle is wired, and the user's own screenshot showed a nocx tab titled '✳ Claude Code' — the marker was arriving and we discarded it. No new protocol, no shell hooks, nothing to wait for.

'permission' is the state worth the loudest treatment: the agent is blocked on a question, which is strictly more urgent than 'finished'.

Two design lessons worth copying from Orca's comments, both learned the hard way there:
- It keeps the title layer and the agent-hook layer as SEPARATE evidence, because consumers combine them differently, and a single merged status silently changes behaviour.
- 'Evidence that something runs is not proof of who': it splits activity classification from agent identity, since a bare spinner says something is working but not what. Do not collapse the two.

Relationship to nocx-5mn.4 (OSC 133): complementary, not competing. OSC 133 D marks SHELL command boundaries — the build finished, claude exited. Title status covers what happens INSIDE one long-running command, which is exactly the Claude Code case OSC 133 cannot see. Build both; they answer different questions.
close_reason: Solved by the title-status layer: a braille spinner means working, Claude Code's ✳ means waiting, and a waiting background tab lights the underline. The OSC 133 dependency was my own modelling error — those markers are complementary (they cover shell command boundaries, which cannot see inside a long-running agent) and remain as nocx-5mn.4, not a blocker for this.

title: Tab title goes blank when a TUI exits (empty OSC 0/2 is taken literally)
description: Run claude code in a tab and exit it: the tab label becomes empty. On exit the program emits an OSC 0/2 with an empty string to clear the title, and Tab.updateTitle writes it straight into textContent, so the tab loses its name and cannot be identified. An empty or whitespace-only title must be ignored and the tab must fall back to its default name.
acceptance_criteria: After a TUI that clears the title exits, the tab shows its fallback name rather than nothing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Frameless window: tabs live in the title bar (Tabby-style)
description: Tabby has no separate title bar: the tab strip IS the title bar, with the macOS traffic lights inset to the left of the first tab. nocx currently renders the native Wails title bar (Title: "nocx" in main.go) with the tab strip as a second row below it, which is the biggest structural difference from Tabby and wastes ~28px of vertical space. Needs Wails Frameless plus the macOS titlebar options (TitleBarHiddenInset / traffic-light inset), a -webkit-app-region drag area on the empty part of the tab strip, and left padding so the tabs clear the traffic lights. Overlaps the app-shell work in nocx-8yg.9 — do them together or sequence deliberately.
acceptance_criteria: The window has no separate native title bar; tabs sit in the title bar area with the traffic lights inset to their left; dragging the empty part of the strip moves the window.
close_reason: Landed in 2c02a46 (commit body already said 'Closes nocx-cpp' but the bead was never closed). Frameless via mac.TitleBarHidden; .tabbar is the title bar with 78px left padding and --wails-draggable: drag, children set back to no-drag. Deviation from the acceptance wording: traffic lights are NOT inset — TitleBarHiddenInset's NSToolbar broke deminiaturize (nocx-dqg, P0), so TitleBarHidden was chosen and the padding clears the lights at their default position.

title: Spine: name the frontend as a first-class quality surface in architecture.md
description: docs/architecture.md:172 Testing strategy enumerates Go surfaces only — 'unit tests per module against interfaces with injected fakes; integration tests across the transport boundary and the session/PTY path'. The module map describes frontend modules (terminal, ui, ipc) with their SRP, but the testing strategy never names them, so a literal reader can conclude the frontend is not a test surface. That gap is how a P0 defect (ipc.ts connect() never resolving) reached review with every gate green. Rewrite the Testing strategy and Quality gates paragraphs to cover the frontend explicitly: tests, lint and formatting on equal footing with Go. AGENTS.md requires changing the spine deliberately rather than routing around it.
acceptance_criteria: architecture.md states frontend tests/lint/format as mandatory; AGENTS.md and README agree with it.
close_reason: Control plane + session registry landed and reviewed over four rounds. JSON-RPC 2.0 open/close/resize + exit notification over text frames; binary data plane framed as version|msgType|16-byte session-id|payload with the metadata type reserved; server-authoritative ids from crypto/rand; PTY created at open's size (proven end-to-end via stty size); real session.Reg behind an injected PTYFactory (AD-8), concrete wiring at the composition root only. Spine updated: frontend is a peer quality surface, CI claims corrected to release-only. 64 tests passing, all gates green.

title: Wire frontend test/lint/format into all three enforcement points
description: The pre-commit hook, make ci and .github/workflows/ci.yml each run only npx tsc --noEmit (plus npm run build) for the frontend. Once the test harness (nocx-tqf) and eslint/prettier (see sibling) exist, add them to all three so the frontend is gated exactly like Go. Per the user's decision the hook must FAIL, not SKIP, when frontend/node_modules is absent — the same way it already fails on a missing gofumpt; the SKIP was a concession to the frontend being second-class. Update the README Quality gates matrix, which currently has no test/lint/format rows for the frontend at all.
acceptance_criteria: Hook, make ci and CI each run frontend test + lint + format:check; README matrix matches reality; hook fails with an actionable message when node_modules is missing.
close_reason: Frontend gated exactly like Go: eslint+prettier+vitest wired into pre-commit, make ci and CI; 39 frontend tests; connect() regression mutation-verified; golden wire vector pinned on both sides.

title: Frontend linter + formatter on equal footing with Go
description: Go has golangci-lint (strict) and gofumpt enforced from every commit; the frontend has neither. tsc --noEmit checks types only — it is the frontend's go vet, not its linter, and not a formatter at all. Add eslint (with typescript-eslint) and prettier to frontend/, configured to match the existing code style rather than reflowing the whole tree, so a diff stays reviewable. Both must be runnable as npm scripts.
acceptance_criteria: npm run lint and npm run format:check exist in frontend/package.json, both pass on the current tree, and a deliberately mis-formatted file fails format:check.
close_reason: Frontend gated exactly like Go: eslint+prettier+vitest wired into pre-commit, make ci and CI; 39 frontend tests; connect() regression mutation-verified; golden wire vector pinned on both sides.

title: Frontend has no test harness — a P0 defect shipped past every gate
description: During nocx-2ho.2 review the coordinator found that ipc.ts connect() returned a promise that never resolved, so tabs.ts hung on await and no terminal could ever appear. gofumpt, golangci-lint, go test -race, tsc --noEmit and npm run build were all green — none of them can execute frontend code. The Go side has 30 tests; the frontend has zero. Any behavioural regression in ipc.ts/tabs.ts/renderers reaches the user. Needs a runtime test harness (vitest is the default for a Vite project) covering at minimum: the connect->open->sessionId lifecycle, frame encode/decode against the Go wire contract in internal/transport/frame.go, and the streaming-TextDecoder split-UTF-8 case from nocx-ao7.
acceptance_criteria: A frontend test command exists, runs in the pre-commit hook and in CI, and a test fails if connect() stops resolving.
close_reason: Frontend gated exactly like Go: eslint+prettier+vitest wired into pre-commit, make ci and CI; 39 frontend tests; connect() regression mutation-verified; golden wire vector pinned on both sides.

title: Drop the ghostty-web dependency; rewrite README for contributors
description: User decision 2026-07-21: ghostty-web is not part of the project. Removed the library (renderers/ghostty.ts, console-filter.ts which existed solely as its log-spam workaround, package.json/lock) and scrubbed it from AGENTS.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/vision.md. ADR-0001 deliberately keeps its ghostty-web content — it is the dated record of why xterm.js won. Competitor 'Ghostty' positioning in vision.md/README kept: that is product framing, not a technology choice. TerminalRenderer + wterm kept so the VT engine stays swappable. README rewritten from stale 'early planning' prose into a working contributor guide: prerequisites, make hooks first, quality gates, beads workflow, sources of truth, layout, verified licenses.
close_reason: Done and verified by the coordinator: zero ghostty-web library references outside docs/decisions/, all grep survivors are competitor positioning; ADR-0001 untouched; TerminalRenderer + wterm intact; pre-commit hook green (gofumpt, golangci-lint, go test -race, tsc); npm run build succeeds. Not committed — conservative profile.

title: Verify the first GitHub Actions run is actually green
description: CI was authored and passes actionlint, but has never executed — no push has happened. Unverified pairings that can only fail on a real runner: golangci-lint-action@v4 driving golangci-lint v1.64.8; setup-go resolving go-version 1.26 on macos-latest; npm ci + tsc + vite build on the ubuntu frontend job; whether go test -race ./... (internal/pty spawns real shells via creack/pty) is stable on a GitHub macOS runner. Watch the first run and fix whatever breaks.
acceptance_criteria: First Actions run on main is green, or the failures are fixed and a subsequent run is green.
close_reason: Run 29822238195 (workflow_dispatch on main) green: backend 2m30s — gofumpt, golangci-lint v1.64.8, go build, go test -race all pass; frontend npm ci + tsc + vite build pass. Root cause of the first failure was golangci-lint-action@v4 shipping a Go-1.24-built binary against go.mod's go 1.26; fixed in 0adab78 by installing the linter with go install under setup-go's Go 1.26.

title: [bake-off] ghostty-web: seams between cells on Retina — canvas-2d fills fractional cell rects, no font size avoids it
description: Big block glyphs render with a visible grid of seams in the ghostty-web tab; xterm.js draws the same art solid. Cause: ghostty-web does ctx.scale(devicePixelRatio) then fillRect(x, y, metrics.width, metrics.height) in CSS pixels, so every cell edge lands between physical pixels and gets antialiased. Reproduced in isolation without WASM: adjacent fillRects of 8.4 CSS px at DPR 2 show seams, 9.0 CSS px are solid. Not fixable by configuration — the font stack's advance/fontSize ratio is 0.6021, so no integer font size from 12 to 20 yields an integer device-pixel cell width. There is also no WebGL path to switch to: the library contains zero webgl/gpu references, canvas-2d only. Same root class as nocx-4wk (blur from imageSmoothing/DPR). Fixing it would mean patching ghostty-web to snap cell metrics to whole device pixels.
notes: CORRECTION: 'not fixable by configuration' was wrong — only integer font sizes were tested. The advance is exactly linear (0.60205em/cell), so fractional sizes do land the cell on whole device pixels: 14.12 -> 17.002 device px, 16.61 -> 20.000 device px at DPR 2. FONT_SIZE set to 14.12 to test. Still unverified: cell HEIGHT (horizontal seams) is derived from font metrics/LINE_HEIGHT and was not measured, and this uses measureText('M') which may differ from ghostty-web's internal metric. Also note the deeper option: ghostty-web's WASM core exposes a full renderer-facing API (getLine/getViewport/isRowDirty/markClean/needsFullRedraw/getCursor/getColors), so a custom WebGL renderer on top of the ghostty VT core is possible — it just means writing from scratch what xterm.js's WebglAddon already provides.
close_reason: ghostty-web dropped from the project (user decision 2026-07-21). These three bugs are ghostty-web-specific rendering defects (imageSmoothing/DPR blur, Retina cell seams from fractional canvas-2d rects, scroll reset on new output) and no longer describe any code we ship. xterm.js is the VT frontend per ADR-0001.

title: [bake-off] ghostty-web resets scroll position to bottom on new output
description: Observed in hermes: scrolling up in the ghostty-web tab is undone by the next chunk of output, so the view is constantly thrown back to the bottom. xterm.js holds the user's scroll position under the same load. For an agent terminal whose status line ticks every second this makes scrollback effectively unusable. Not reproduced in an automated harness yet — headless virtual-time racing the WASM load made the measurement flaky — so this rests on direct observation. Renderer-specific, so it is a genuine bake-off differentiator against ghostty-web.
close_reason: ghostty-web dropped from the project (user decision 2026-07-21). These three bugs are ghostty-web-specific rendering defects (imageSmoothing/DPR blur, Retina cell seams from fractional canvas-2d rects, scroll reset on new output) and no longer describe any code we ship. xterm.js is the VT frontend per ADR-0001.

title: [bug] Resize forwarded to PTY on every intermediate grid size — SIGWINCH storm shreds TUIs
description: tabs.ts forwarded every renderer onResize straight to ws.sendResize with no debounce and no dedupe, so dragging a window edge walks the PTY through every intermediate grid size. Each one is a SIGWINCH and a full TUI repaint for a size that is already stale — visible as the screen falling apart during resize, identically in all three renderers (shared code, not the engines). Fix: skip unchanged cols/rows and debounce the PTY notification by RESIZE_SETTLE_MS (80ms); local fitting stays immediate.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging the window edge produces one PTY resize on settle, not one per intermediate size; TUI redraws cleanly
close_reason: Fixed in frontend/src/tabs.ts: dedupe unchanged grid sizes + 80ms trailing debounce before notifying the PTY.

title: [bug] WS frames decoded with a fresh TextDecoder — split UTF-8 sequences become U+FFFD
description: ipc.ts decoded every WebSocket frame with 'new TextDecoder().decode(buf)'. A PTY read ends at an arbitrary byte offset, so multi-byte UTF-8 routinely straddles two frames; a per-frame decoder severs the sequence and emits U+FFFD for each half. U+FFFD renders as a question mark in a diamond, identically in every renderer, so it reads as a font/glyph bug and sent the renderer bake-off chasing ghosts. Reproduced live against the real PTY+WS: braille art through a 40-col PTY gave 10x U+FFFD with the old path, 0 with a single streaming decoder. Fix: one TextDecoder per connection, decode(buf, {stream:true}).
acceptance_criteria: Multi-byte UTF-8 split across WS frames renders intact; verified end-to-end against a live PTY
close_reason: Fixed in frontend/src/ipc.ts: one TextDecoder per connection with {stream:true}. Verified end-to-end against a live PTY — 10x U+FFFD before, 0 after.

title: [bug] PTY inherits no locale when app is launched from Finder → TUIs downgrade UTF-8 to '?'
description: pty_local.go sets only TERM: cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "TERM=xterm-256color"). A macOS .app launched from Finder/Dock has no LANG/LC_* in its environment, so the child shell has no locale. Python/Rich/prompt_toolkit TUIs then compute a non-UTF-8 stdout encoding and encode with errors='replace', which emits literal '?' bytes for every non-ASCII glyph — identical in every renderer, so it masquerades as a font bug. Launching via 'wails dev' from a terminal hides this because LANG is inherited. Fix: default LANG/LC_CTYPE to a UTF-8 locale in NewLocal when absent.
acceptance_criteria: Shell spawned by a Finder-launched nocx.app reports a UTF-8 locale; non-ASCII TUI output renders without '?' substitution
close_reason: Fixed in internal/pty/pty_local.go: withUTF8Locale() defaults LANG=en_US.UTF-8 when the inherited environment states no locale at all (LC_ALL/LC_CTYPE/LANG all absent), which is the Finder/Dock launch case. An inherited locale is never overridden, including a deliberate LANG=C. Table-driven test covers all five cases; go test -race, gofumpt and golangci-lint all green.

title: Renderer bake-off: tabbed A/B harness (ghostty-web vs xterm.js vs wterm)
description: Cannot pick a VT frontend by staring at one at a time. Put each renderer behind its own tab, each with its own PTY session (backend already spawns one PTY per WS connection), so the same workload can be run in each and compared side by side. Feeds the renderer decision that nocx-dej (ghostty-web API spike) and nocx-4wk (render bugs) both hang on.

close_reason: Bake-off harness delivered its purpose — three renderers side by side, each with its own live PTY, drove the renderer decision. Tabs stay in the codebase for re-testing future candidates.

title: M0 render (data-backed): blur=imageSmoothing reset on resize; top-clip=canvas 6px taller than container; scroll needs instrumentation

TOP-CLIP: canvas CSS height 930 is 6px taller than #terminal container 924 (overflow:hidden), and 17px narrower -> non-integer rows -> partial row. title: M0 agent-TUI render: blurry after fit() (DPR) + alt-screen scroll snaps to bottom
description: Two frontend/ghostty-web issues (plain terminal is fine). (1) Text became blurry after the scroll fix added terminal.fit() in main.ts -> canvas likely no longer sized for devicePixelRatio on resize, or fit() runs before layout. PTY winsize stays 80x24 while ghostty-web renders the real window size -> agent TUIs read the wrong winsize via ioctl -> full-screen redraw overflows -> constant downward scroll.

description: AD-6/AD-7. Authoritative registry; one goroutine per session; lifecycle.

JSON-RPC 2.0 open/close/resize + exit notification over text frames; binary data plane framed as version|msgType|16-byte session-id|payload with the metadata type reserved; server-authoritative ids from crypto/rand; PTY created at open's size (proven end-to-end via stty size); real session.Reg behind an injected PTYFactory (AD-8), concrete wiring at the composition root only. Spine updated: frontend is a peer quality surface, CI claims corrected to release-only. 64 tests passing, all gates green.

description: AD-1. Route binary frames by 16-byte session-id; concurrent sessions.

description: AD-10. Bounded credit; throttle PTY/SSH read when full; lossless+ordered; per-session fairness.

JSON-RPC 2.0 open/close/resize + exit notification over text frames; binary data plane framed as version|msgType|16-byte session-id|payload with the metadata type reserved; server-authoritative ids from crypto/rand; PTY created at open's size (proven end-to-end via stty size); real session.Reg behind an injected PTYFactory (AD-8), concrete wiring at the composition root only. Spine updated: frontend is a peer quality surface, CI claims corrected to release-only. 64 tests passing, all gates green.

title: [epic] Delete wterm and make the renderer seam honest
description:
Rescoped 2026-07-26. This was 'Terminal core', an area rather than a deliverable — it collected anything touching the renderer and could never close. Its unrelated child nocx-3cc (OSC 52 grants) moved to nocx-ywhp, where a permission model belongs.

What is left is one coherent job: the xterm-vs-wterm bake-off is settled (ADR-0001), and the loser is still in the tree, still advertised through the TerminalRenderer interface, and still degrading behaviour.

- nocx-k7kq: delete the wterm renderer.
- nocx-au6: TerminalRenderer advertises capabilities wterm silently does not have — the seam lies about what a renderer can do.
- nocx-id3: wterm translates the wheel to arrow keys and scrolls prompt history instead of the buffer.
- nocx-dau: text squeezes for a frame when a window resize starts.

nocx-id3 will likely close as won't-fix once the renderer is gone; record that outcome rather than deleting the bead, so the bake-off's findings stay readable.

DONE WHEN: no wterm code remains, TerminalRenderer advertises only capabilities the surviving renderer actually has, and resizing does not visibly squeeze text.
acceptance_criteria: no wterm code remains, TerminalRenderer advertises only capabilities the surviving renderer actually has, and resizing does not visibly squeeze text.
close_reason:
Epic complete: 7/7. wterm is gone and the renderer seam no longer lies.

nocx-k7kq deleted wterm.ts, the vestigial factory and the @wterm/dom dependency — but the part that mattered was types.ts: 8 concession comments removed and 8 members that were optional ONLY to accommodate wterm made non-optional. That is what retired nocx-au6 properly rather than by deleting the complaint, and the payoff showed downstream where gutter.ts dropped its optional calls and a magic 'cellHeight ?? 15' fallback that existed only because wterm might not supply one. ADR-0001 got a visible superseding note rather than a quietly rewritten sentence. nocx-id3 closed because its subject ceased to exist.

nocx-dau, the last child, turned out to be caused by the geometry rewrite rather than by what it described — and by my own brief, which asked for rAF coalescing that ResizeObserver already does, adding a frame of delay that WAS the squeeze.

Also removed a live defect, not just dead code: wterm's fitViewport approximated cell width as a full em where monospace advance is nearer 0.6em, so its computed columns were materially wrong.

Not merged to main.

title: The nocxify journey proves the second connection again
description:
The nocxify journey lost the assertions that watched shell.launcherCommand
and the compact installed carrier when nocx-292k landed: both watched a
deleted RPC and a delivery path selected by an installed fact that has no
production writer, so leaving them would have timed out or preserved a test
narrative for functionality that no longer exists.

What the journey still proves is the user-visible half — the frozen local
block, remote blocks from the first prompt, the exit back to local, the auth
failure, rc files intact, one verified generation. What it no longer proves
is that the SECOND connection is cheaper than the first.

Depends on the installed-fact writer (blocker A): until facts are recorded,
there is no compact path to assert.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The journey asserts, at the wire or filesystem level, that a second
  connection to the same host is integrated from its first prompt by a
  route distinguishable from the first connection.
- No assertion references shell.launcherCommand, shell.environmentObserved
  or the .nocx/run staging directory.

title: The insert toast still asks for the Enter that is now sent with the value
description:
After fc189136 the newline goes with the resolved value — picking a secret at a password prompt IS the answer to it. The toast still read 'Secret inserted — press Enter to send it', which asks for a keystroke that now submits a second, empty line.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. At a password prompt, open the tab-strip key icon and pick a secret.
2. The far side already received the answer, and the toast asks for Enter.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The toast reports a completed send and asks for no keystroke.
- It still says something, rather than nothing: a password prompt echoes nothing, and an answer the user cannot see is an answer they give twice.
close_reason: Landed in 399574d4: the toast reports a completed send.

title: Answer ssh's password prompt through nocx, via SSH_ASKPASS rather than the tty
description:
Owner, 2026-08-10: "can we intercept the password prompt and show a dialog
like the vault one? Or at least let me paste a password from the vault."

Today a hand-typed `ssh` to a password host is answered in the pty by the ssh
client itself. nocx has a password dialog and a vault full of credentials,
and neither is reachable from there — while a PROFILE connection uses both,
because the backend owns that transport.

## Why this is now possible without sniffing the stream

nocx already rewrites the command for a nested ssh (ADR-0022), so it composes
the argv. OpenSSH has a supported seam for exactly this: SSH_ASKPASS plus
SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force makes the client call a helper program instead of
reading the tty. The composer can point that at a nocx helper, which asks the
backend over a channel and returns the answer.

That keeps the whole thing inside the architecture: no OSC parsing, no
matching "password:" in the byte stream (AD-6, ADR-0004), no timing guess
about when the prompt appears. The client asks; we answer.

It also opens the useful half of the request: the destination is known before
the connection (host/user ride the domain_request, ADR-0025), so nocx can
look for a matching stored secret and offer it — the same lookup the profile
path already does.

## Open questions for the brief

- Where the helper lives and how it authenticates back to the backend. It
  runs on the LOCAL machine as the user, so the lifecycle channel is not
  automatically the right carrier.
- Whether a no-match falls back to the client`s own tty prompt (it must — a
  helper that fails must not make the host unreachable).
- Whether an answer may be remembered, and under whose consent. The vault has
  a named-create surface (ADR-0016/0017) the profile path already uses.
- SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE is OpenSSH 8.4+; older clients need the fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Typing `ssh host` for a destination with a stored secret offers it through
  the same dialog the vault uses, and the session logs in without the user
  typing the password.
- With no stored secret, the user gets nocx`s prompt and may choose to
  remember the answer.
- With the helper unavailable or refused, the ssh client prompts on the tty
  exactly as it does today.
- Nothing anywhere matches on the word "password" in the output stream.
close_reason: Merged into nocx-jee1 by owner decision 2026-08-10: same askpass seam, and AGENTS.md gives one behaviour one owner. Everything 5175 carried that jee1 did not — the ADR-0022 argv composition, the ADR-0025 pre-connection destination, the OpenSSH 8.4+ bound, the local-helper authentication question and the tty fallback — is recorded on jee1 as a comment. jee1 covers sudo and ssh together and is P1.

title: A nested ssh session does not say which host it is on
description:
Owner, 2026-08-10: inside a hand-typed `ssh`, nothing on screen says the
session is on another machine. The cwd chip reads `home/pi` — correct, and
indistinguishable from a local /home/pi.

A profile-opened ssh tab carries the destination in its tab title
(root@ct-ziti-tunneler). A nested one carries nothing: same tab, same title,
same chip vocabulary, and the only hint is the shell prompt the far host
happens to print.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a local tab, `ssh pi@192.168.0.93`, log in.
2. Run `pwd`. The block chip says `home/pi`.
3. Nothing distinguishes this from a local session in /home/pi.

## Why it matters beyond cosmetics

This is the "which machine am I about to run this on" question, and the
answer is currently the user`s memory. The information exists and is
authenticated — the child domain carries host and user (ADR-0025: the
domain_request carries exactly the destination), so the projection can state
it without inferring anything from the stream.

## Deliberately open

Where it belongs — the block chip, the pane`s capability rail, the tab title,
or more than one — is a design question, not a fix. The rail already states
what is true at the prompt (nocx-4t37.2) and is the natural candidate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A nested session states its destination somewhere a user reading the pane
  cannot miss.
- It is derived from the active domain, never from the prompt text or any
  other stream-derived guess (AD-6).
- Returning to the parent removes it in the same instant the domain does.
close_reason:
Fixed in 519c46f4. The destination now rides the published fact and the renderer states it.

Where it was stuck: domain_request already carried host/user/port (ADR-0025) and the value stopped at the grant seam. frontend/src/lifecycle/domain-environment.ts said so outright on its 'host' field — a child domain has no authenticated host source and shows none until one exists. This bead is that source.

Boundary: publishing it is inside ADR-0024 decision 7, not against it. What may never cross is the per-epoch capability and raw frames; schema-checked facts crossing is the point of the boundary. It carries no authority — domain id and epoch remain the only authority the renderer gets — and nothing is derived from prompt text (AD-6).

One owner: the publisher records it at the grant seam, the single point where the child's identity and its destination are both in hand. The kernel deliberately does not keep it.

Where it shows: the environment projection seeds an ssh child's record with host, user, isLocal=false and the destination as the tab title — the same thing the lane seed already does for a profile-opened ssh session, which is what the owner asked for ('as for the ssh we get from quick connect'). Everything downstream was already wired to that one projection, so the block header chip, the editor location chip, the tooltip and the tab all name it through the derivation they always shared. It disappears in the same fact the domain does.

Proven three ways: internal/lifecyclepub/grant_test.go drives the real grant seam; TestLifecycleChanged_DTOConformsToContract covers both shapes against the schema; the live-sshd assembly test asserts the destination reaches the fact for a child established over a real ssh client against a real sshd.

title: Transport tests flake at their 5s bound under container load
description:
Observed 2026-08-10 while running the containerized suite repeatedly for
nocx-beib: two runs out of four failed in internal/transport, each at exactly
its 5.00s bound, and a different test each time
(TestLifecycleChanged_DeadSessionGetsNoRecoveryClaim,
TestGitChanged_OverTheWireConformsToContract). Both pass locally and both
pass in the container on a clean tree and on repeat runs, and the change
under test touched only shell scripts, which these tests never execute.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run .githooks/containerized-tests.sh (go_test_containerized) several
   times on a loaded machine.
2. Occasionally one transport test fails after exactly its wait bound.

## Why it matters

A suite that fails at random teaches people to re-run rather than to read,
which is how a real failure gets waved through. The bound is the suspect: a
fixed 5s wait for a published fact is a timing assumption about a machine
under unknown load, not about the code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The transport waits are condition-based rather than a fixed sleep-to-bound,
  or the bound is derived from something the test controls.
- Twenty consecutive containerized runs are green.

title: Shift+Enter is indistinguishable from Enter, so no program can bind it
description:
Reported by the owner, 2026-08-09: Shift+Enter does not insert a newline in omp, and the same in other TUIs.

Cause: while a program owns the keyboard the keys go through xterm's default handler, and nocx installs no custom key handling — there is no attachCustomKeyEventHandler, no modifyOtherKeys and no CSI-u / kitty keyboard protocol anywhere in frontend/src/renderers/xterm.ts. xterm's default sends a bare CR for Enter and does not encode the shift modifier, so the program receives exactly the same byte for Enter and for Shift+Enter and cannot tell them apart. This is not omp's defect: it is what the terminal does or does not send.

The fix is a choice, and it should be made deliberately rather than by picking the first sequence that makes omp work: the two conventions are the legacy 'ESC CR' that many editors accept, and a proper modifier encoding (xterm's modifyOtherKeys, or the kitty keyboard protocol) which programs negotiate and which also fixes every other unencodable chord rather than this one. Whichever is chosen, say why at the site and say what the other one would have bought.

nocx's own editor is unaffected — it handles Enter/Shift+Enter itself (editor.ts:588) — so this is strictly about the raw path while a program owns the pane.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run omp (or any TUI that binds Shift+Enter to 'insert newline') in an integrated session.
2. Press Shift+Enter.
3. Observed: it behaves exactly like Enter — the message is submitted instead of a newline inserted.

## Acceptance Criteria

A program running in the pane can distinguish Shift+Enter from Enter, proven by a test asserting the bytes nocx writes to the pty for each. The chosen mechanism is recorded at the site with the alternative named. If a negotiated protocol is chosen, the default (nothing negotiated) still behaves exactly as today, so no existing program changes behaviour.
close_reason: Shift+Enter is re-encoded as ESC CR through xterm's custom key handler; Enter stays a bare CR. Legacy convention chosen over modifyOtherKeys/kitty because xterm.js 5.5.0 ships neither and hand-rolling a negotiation beside a library that will have one is what the repo's reuse rule forbids — reasoning and the Alt+Enter collision recorded at the site. Neighbouring chords pinned by tests. Not verified against a real TUI: the proof is byte-level.

title: Transport notification tests time out under container load — three different tests so far
description:
Seen four times during the nocx-u7uh epic's gate runs, always as an exact 5.00s 'timed out waiting for <x> notification' and never as a logic failure:

- TestGitChanged_OverTheWireConformsToContract
- TestLifecycleChanged_DeadSessionGetsNoRecoveryClaim
- TestConnectionsPasswordRequest_OverTheWireConformsToContract
- once, internal/lifecyclechannel as a whole

Each passes in isolation and on re-run; a full 'go test -race ./...' in the pre-commit container passes on the same tree that just failed. So the notification wait (5s) is not generous enough for the container under full-suite parallel load, and the failure is indistinguishable from a real regression at the moment it appears — which is the expensive part: a coordinator bisecting one of these spends a wave measuring noise. It also erodes the gate: a red run that is 'probably the flake' is a gate nobody trusts.

Note TestLifecycleChanged_DeadSessionGetsNoRecoveryClaim additionally fails reproducibly under -count=2 while passing under -count=1, so at least one of these is not idempotent within a process — that is a separate, findable defect rather than pure timing.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the pre-commit hook's containerized 'go test -race ./...' on a loaded machine, repeatedly.
2. Observed: one of the tests above fails with an exact 5.00s notification timeout.
3. Re-run the same package in isolation: passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

The notification waits no longer fail under container load — either the wait is derived from a documented budget rather than a bare 5s literal, or the tests stop racing the runtime. The non-idempotence of TestLifecycleChanged_DeadSessionGetsNoRecoveryClaim under -count=2 is diagnosed and fixed rather than papered over by a longer timeout. Proven by a repeated full containerized run (>=5 consecutive) staying green on a loaded machine.

title: su nested child domain is wired on both tiers but never proven on a pty
description:
nocx-u7uh.11 (bash) and nocx-u7uh.28 (zsh) both prove the nested child domain end to end for 'sudo' on a real pty, and nocx-u7uh.29 proves 'ssh' as a live assembly against a real sshd. 'su' is wired on both tiers — detected, requested, granted, launched — and has no pty-level proof on either.

su is not sudo: it crosses the privilege boundary differently, many implementations preserve descriptors while resetting the environment, and none promise it. The brief for nocx-u7uh.11 said explicitly 'test it; never infer success from inheritance', and that half is outstanding.

## Acceptance Criteria

A test on a real pty watches a parent enter 'su' and the child establish its own authenticated domain, on both the bash and zsh tiers, the way TestBashNestedChildDomain and TestZshNestedChildDomain do for sudo. Where the platform's su does not preserve the descriptor, the honest conventional fallback is asserted instead — and which platforms fall in which bucket is written down where the launcher decides.
close_reason: Four real-pty tests prove su's nested child domain: bash and zsh happy paths (completion asserted on the CHILD's domain, parent re-activates only through an authenticated activation), an auth-refused stillborn that injects a late frame from the child that never established and counts its rejection, and a descriptor-closed case asserting the conventional degrade. Real su descriptor preservation established by reading util-linux 2.42.2, shadow 4.19.4 and the BSD/macOS lineage AND by measuring the shadow su on this host preserving fd 7 through the exact launcher line — recorded at the launcher decision site, together with the fact that none of them promises it.

title: The ssh child domain is proven in pieces, never end to end against a real sshd
description:
nocx-u7uh.11 proved every piece of the ssh child path separately — the composed command line evals under bash and carries the -R byte-exact (TestComposeSSHChildLine_*), the loopback listener transport works, the in-band installer works, the kernel grant flow works — but never the combination: a real ssh client reaching a real sshd over the composed line, the reverse forward terminating at the listener, and the remote shell's hello establishing the child.

The live_sshd fixture is where this belongs (internal/app/live_sshd_test.go already drives a real sshd through the production composition). The gap that stopped it: the fixture's client key has to reach the composed line's ssh, and domain_request carries only host/user/port — typed options such as -i are deliberately not reproduced, which is a documented limit of the request shape rather than an oversight.

Until this lands, 'ssh establishes an authenticated child domain' is an assembly of proven parts, not a proven assembly.

## Acceptance Criteria

An automated test drives a real ssh client against the live sshd fixture over the composed child line and asserts the child domain reaches Established through its own hello on the reverse-forwarded transport, that the parent is Suspended for the whole interval, and that the parent re-activates only through an authenticated activation. Whether domain_request should carry the user's typed ssh options is DECIDED and written down — either the request shape grows or the limit is stated where a reader of the composer will find it.
close_reason: The ssh child is now proven as an assembly against the live sshd fixture, not as parts: the -R forward terminates at the lifecycle listener and the far shell's own hello establishes the child, parent Suspended throughout, re-activating only via authenticated activation; forwarding-refused, stillborn and late-frame paths covered. Found three defects no per-piece test could see: -t never allocates the remote pty (now -tt), the child's capability was never set on the in-band plan (capability-free integration), and the grant builder captured a nil publisher. Option question decided in ADR-0025.

title: A ready prompt stays unstructured until the first command starts
description:
Found by the nocx-u7uh.25 worker and deliberately left.

After nocx-u7uh.25 the block model is no longer torn down on every fact, but a session sitting at a ready prompt with no command yet is still in the unstructured mode it was left in — nothing moves it to the idle/structured layout until the first command starts and opens a block. The pre-ADR-0024 code called setIdle at that point; the ADR rework dropped it.

Consequence: the first impression of an integrated session is a conventional flat grid, and the structure only appears once the user has run something. Cosmetic rather than functional, which is why it was left rather than folded into .25.

Decide whether a ready prompt with a live domain should present the idle structured layout, and if so restore that call with the same integrated predicate .25 used.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open an integrated session and wait at the prompt without running anything.
2. Observed: the pane is in the unstructured full-pane layout.
3. Expected (to be confirmed): a live domain at a ready prompt presents the idle structured layout.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded on what a ready prompt with a live domain should present, and the code matches it: either the idle structured layout is restored at prompt_ready, or the comment says why unstructured-until-first-command is correct.
close_reason: Decision recorded: YES, a ready prompt with a live domain presents the idle structured layout — ADR-0024 §4 is what entitles it, and flat-until-first-command was an implementation accident of the ADR rework. setIdle restored in the lifecycle onChange prompt_ready branch.

title: Alt-screen exit leaves an integrated session unstructured until the next command
description:
Found by the nocx-u7uh.25 worker and deliberately left, so it does not evaporate.

renderer.onBufferChange in frontend/src/terminal-content.ts calls scrollback.setUnstructured() unconditionally when leaving the alternate buffer. It is the same unconditional shape nocx-u7uh.25 fixed one call site up, and historically it was gated on the OSC-133 integration latch that ADR-0024 deleted.

Consequence: an integrated session that runs an alt-screen program (vim, less, top) comes back to a flat unstructured grid and stays there until the next command starts, instead of returning to the structured block layout its live domain entitles it to.

The fix is presumably the same predicate nocx-u7uh.25 used — shellStateFromLifecycle(state) !== 'integrated' — but confirm that against the fullscreen/exitFullscreen path before assuming it, because the alt-screen exit has ordering constraints setUnstructured declines while an alt-screen program owns the pane.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open an integrated session and confirm blocks appear for a command.
2. Run an alt-screen program (e.g. vim) and quit it.
3. Observed: the pane is a flat unstructured grid; no block framing until the next command starts.
4. Expected: leaving the alternate buffer returns the session to the structured block layout.
acceptance_criteria: Leaving the alternate buffer in an integrated session restores the structured block layout rather than a flat grid, and a conventional session still stays unstructured on the same path. Proven in the real UI.
close_reason: Leaving the alternate buffer asks the one existing integrated predicate: a live domain returns to the structured block layout (idle, or running while an attempt is in flight), a conventional session still lands unstructured. Four tests, both directions.

title: Recovery fence: how a Lost session becomes a conventional terminal
description:
Decided during nocx-u7uh.15. ADR-0024 decision 8 fixes the PROPERTY (restoration must be acknowledged before a session is treated as a usable conventional terminal) and deliberately leaves the MECHANISM open. The mechanism chosen: a composite ACK on decision 1's rendezvous carve-out — the shell emits a one-shot recovery fence, pre-provisioned during the authenticated bootstrap, after restoring its native PS1; the renderer matches the fence without inspecting the grid and acks only once the conventional presentation is also applied; the lane goes Lost -> Native while the domain stays permanently Lost.

Rejected alternatives and why: (a) the renderer OBSERVING a repainted native prompt in the grid — untrusted inference, reintroduces the render-state -> control-plane edge this epic exists to sever; (b) the renderer acking only that it APPLIED the conventional presentation — acks the wrong thing, leaves ADR-0024:439's feared state (suppressed prompt taking raw input) reachable.

Why the pre-shared nonce is not a new stream-derived authority edge: a forged recovery fence can only force a transition to native mode, which ADR-0024:472 already accepts as a bounded availability loss.

This bead is the OPEN QUESTION for the owner: does this belong in docs/lifecycle-protocol.md (worker .15 is writing it there) or as an amendment to ADR-0024 itself? Editing the ADR is the owner's call, so .15 was told not to.
acceptance_criteria: The owner decides whether the recovery-fence mechanism is documented in docs/lifecycle-protocol.md or as an amendment to ADR-0024, and the chosen document says so.
close_reason: Owner decided both: the mechanism stays in docs/lifecycle-protocol.md §12.1, which now says it is decision 8's deferred mechanism, and ADR-0024 decision 8 carries a pointer plus the two rejected alternatives.

title: The shell cannot name its active or last-completed attempt in a snapshot
description:
Found by nocx-u7uh.9 while building the recovery. The protocol says a snapshot carries the active attempt and the last completed one; the shell hooks cannot supply them, so every completion lost inside a gap reconciles as unknown even when the shell knows the exit status. That is SAFE — unknown is never success — but it is lossy, and the loss is invisible to the user.

Also open from the same bead: zsh and the POSIX tier do not yet answer a refresh request; only bash does.

## Acceptance Criteria

Per --acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: A snapshot answering a refresh carries active_attempt and last_completed with the shell's own view, and a completion lost inside a corrupted region reconciles to its real status rather than to unknown — including for app-originated attempts, via a per-domain alias recorded only from an authenticated start (kernel applyStart attach branch). Plus: nocx.zsh answers refresh_request the way nocx.bash now does. POSIX sh is deliberately EXCLUDED: nocx.posix:12-22 and ADR-0024:207-208 say the authenticated channel is not implementable in that tier and it needs its own proven adapter (Tier B) or gets nothing — a POSIX host stays a conventional terminal, and the omission is documented in the script rather than faked.
close_reason: Shell names its own attempts (domain-scoped ids); applyStart records an unexported per-attempt alias; applySnapshot resolves through it so a lost completion keeps its real exit status while unknown ids still reconcile to unknown. zsh answers refresh_request; POSIX deliberately excluded per nocx.posix:12-22 and ADR-0024:207-208. No new field crosses JSON-RPC, contracts untouched. Round 2 fixed a cross-domain id collision that broke nested domains on docker exec. Committed 00c14ceb; full pre-commit gate green.

title: Audit every renderer stale-guard for the shared-counter shape the git store had
description:
## Why

Removing the control plane's implicit FIFO (nocx-sfv6) broke the Git panel in a way no Go test could see and no ordering audit found. git-store.ts kept ONE lastAppliedEpoch across three independent facts — status, log and remote. A remote read issued after the log completed before it, bumped the shared counter, and the log's arriving response was discarded as stale. The panel sat in 'idle' forever: no rows, and not even the 'No commits yet' text, because it never learned anything.

The pre-work audit asked 'does the renderer await its mutations before dependent reads' and the answer was yes. That question cannot find this: the dependency was not an await, it was a counter. Any guard of the form 'drop a response whose sequence number is older than the newest applied' assumes responses land in issue order, which the transport no longer promises and ADR-0024 now says so explicitly.

## What to check

Known siblings, none of them yet judged:

- frontend/src/files/files-store.ts — dir.appliedGeneration is per DIRECTORY, which is narrower than the git store's, but six separate call sites write it (446, 460, 470, 489, 912, 1019) against guards at 420, 477, 887, 992. If two different response kinds for one directory can bump it, the same defect is there.
- frontend/src/settings-observer.ts:45 and frontend/src/settings-domain.ts:138 — revision guards. Settings revisions are server-monotonic, which may make them safe; say so with the reason rather than assuming.

Then sweep for the shape rather than the names: any comparison of a stored 'applied/last/expected' number against one carried by an in-flight response.
acceptance_criteria: Every stale-guard in the renderer is either scoped to one class of fact, or documented with why sharing is safe for it. At least one test per guard that is NOT already per-class drives two responses completing in the opposite order to their issue and asserts the older one does not discard the newer — the discriminating shape, not a smoke test.

title: Prove the remote lifecycle channel against a real sshd, and add the zsh net/tcp adapter
description:
nocx-u7uh.4 landed the adapter and proved it against the TunnelConn seam and its tests. It was NOT run against a live remote host and zsh has no net/tcp adapter — the worker said so plainly rather than letting silence imply coverage, which is why this bead exists instead of a surprise later.

## Acceptance Criteria

Per --acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: A run against a real sshd shows a bash shell on a remote host reaching an accepted domain with nothing installed there, and a host with AllowTcpForwarding no falling back to a visible native prompt. Plus a zsh adapter using zmodload zsh/net/tcp, or a written statement of why zsh cannot have one.
close_reason: landed in fa812fda: real sshd proofs plus the zsh ztcp adapter

title: Research: how often is there no transport?
description:
ADR-0024 accepts that POSIX sh remotes, forwarding-disabled hosts and docker exec shells lose enhanced input until Tier B. Whether that is a footnote or a serious regression is a measurement, and the ADR deliberately refuses to guess it from an armchair.

Independent of every other child — it informs the roadmap, not the implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria

Per --acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: A written finding against real hosts the owner actually uses: how many run a POSIX sh login shell, how many set AllowTcpForwarding no, how many sessions are docker exec. Concludes with a recommendation on whether Tier B moves up the roadmap, and files the follow-up bead if so.
notes: Explicitly NON-blocking: ADR-0024 places Tier B in a later epic regardless, so this informs the roadmap and must not silently expand this epic's DONE WHEN halfway through. If the finding is that no-transport is common, it files a follow-up bead — it does not widen nocx-u7uh.
close_reason: landed in 57c7723e: not estimable from data at rest; Tier B stays deferred, probes listed

title: Saturation is visible in the product: a structured retryable error, one central renderer mapping, and a contract schema
description:
A wire error is not product visibility. `dispatcher.ts:234` turns any RPC error
into a rejected promise, so whether the user learns anything depends on each
call site remembering to show it — which is exactly the "soft degrade visible
only in a log" shape AGENTS.md forbids.

A rejected request answers immediately with a stable error:

    {"code": -32001, "message": "Control plane busy",
     "data": {"reason": "control-saturated", "scope": "connection",
              "retryable": true, "retryAfterMs": 250}}

No secret-bearing parameters in `data`; the transport-wide rule that no control
frame is logged verbatim applies here too. A notification with no id gets a
rate-limited `control.saturated` instead, carrying method class and scope only.

One central mapping in the dispatcher turns `data.reason === "control-saturated"`
into a deduplicated toast, so a surface that forgets still degrades visibly.
Individual surfaces may additionally disable an action or retry.

The result shape gets a schema in `contracts/` in this commit, per the wire rule
— `additionalProperties: false` plus explicit `required`, generated renderer
types, and the over-the-wire conformance test off the real socket.

Observability alongside: active work and admission rejections per lane, duration
by non-secret method name, cancellations. No parameters.
acceptance_criteria: Ordinary saturation returns the structured error immediately rather than queueing; the renderer shows it without the calling surface opting in; releasing one worker lets the next request complete. npm run contracts:check passes and the over-the-wire conformance test validates the real payload off the real socket.
notes: 2026-08-08, round 2: the saturation payload reports Admission.Name(). That name is OBSERVATIONAL ONLY — no implementation may branch on it, or the injected-resource design collapses back into the lane enum it replaced.
close_reason:
Landed as cc098df. Wire form (-32004 + data{reason,scope,retryable,retryAfterMs}), two contracts schemas with additionalProperties:false and explicit required, generated renderer types committed, and one central dispatcher mapping that raises a deduplicated sticky toast with zero call-site opt-in. Four acceptance tests: surfaces without opt-in, dedups a burst, re-toasts after the window, leaves an ordinary RPC error alone.

Two properties are structural, not promised: saturationErrorFor takes ONLY a *control.Rejection — no request in the signature, so a request parameter cannot reach the wire — and scope is the admission's own Name, closed server vocabulary set at the composition root.

Worker corrected the brief: -32001 was already vault-sealed, so the code is -32004 (next free after the vault's -32000..-32003). Verified against every code in use.

Coordinator review changed one thing: the lazy toast import swallowed a chunk-load failure with .catch(() => undefined). A notifier that goes silent without a trace is the exact defect this surface exists to prevent, so it logs now.

Deliberately left to nocx-sfv6.5 and recorded there: the OverTheWire contract test (needs a real saturation off a real socket) and the notification emission rate limit. Their baseline entries carry the obligation.

title: enhanced-input spec gates back-to-back submits on output, not on the prompt returning
description:
The gate is on the wrong fact. e2e/enhanced-input.spec.ts:85-97 submits three
commands back to back and, between iterations, waits for the previous
command"s OUTPUT block to be visible before typing the next one. The comment is
explicit that a race is being guarded against — but a visible block means the
output arrived, NOT that the prompt returned and the editor owns input again.
The editor is still hidden for a moment after the output paints.

This is the same defect that made e2e/nocxify-journey.spec.ts fail in CI run
31219714125 (fixed there by routing the four raw keyboard sites through
submitInEditor, which waits for the editor). enhanced-input is green today, so
this is a latent instance, not a current failure.

The repository already owns the right question: `promptReady(page)` in
e2e/harness.ts asserts the editor is visible AND focused. The spec calls it
once at the start and then stops asking.

Caution for whoever takes this: adding promptReady inside the loop asserts
FOCUS as well as visibility, which the spec does not assert today. If the
editor comes back visible but unfocused after a command, this turns a latent
race into a red test — which would itself be a finding worth having, but it
must be confirmed in the container before the change is called done.

## Steps to Reproduce

Read e2e/enhanced-input.spec.ts:85-97. The loop types iteration i+1 gated only
on iteration i"s output block.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each iteration waits for the prompt to be back — the thing it needs — rather
  than for the previous command"s output.
- The wait goes through the existing promptReady helper, not a fourth spelling
  of it.
- Confirmed green in the container and on CI, both engines.

title: the shell scripts ship ~22KB of comments to every remote host, three times over
description:
## Summary

62% of nocx.bash is comments — measured 15,849 of 25,510 bytes, plus 3,176 in
nocx.zsh and 3,004 in nocx.posix. ~22 KB of prose in total, and the remote host
is sent all of it, octal-escaped (~2.4x) and carried more than once, on every
bootstrap. It is never read by anything on the far side.

This is why nocx-z9s9.17 exists: the cap can go no higher than MAX_ARG_STRLEN, so
the only remaining lever is the payload. Stripping comments from the EMBEDDED
copy would free roughly 50 KB of the 118 KB command — enough that script growth
stops being a design constraint for years.

## Why it is not a one-liner

The comments must stay in the repo (they carry the reasoning AGENTS.md exists to
preserve); only the shipped bytes should shrink. That means stripping at embed
time, which touches: the version digest (scripts_version_test.go), the manifest
hashes, publisher byte-identity (design N4, TestStageWritesPayloadByteIdentical),
and the remote install path. The stripper must not corrupt shell syntax — a '#'
inside a string or a here-doc is not a comment.

Alternative worth measuring first: gzip+base64 the bundle and decompress on the
far side, which needs no stripper but assumes gzip/base64 on the remote host.
acceptance_criteria: The bootstrap payload carries no comment text, and the ShellAuto command drops well clear of MAX_ARG_STRLEN. The installed scripts remain byte-identical to what the manifest hashes, and TestStageWritesPayloadByteIdentical still holds.
close_reason: Comment stripper at embed time: bash 42086->15553, zsh 22305->9765, posix 5826->1862; ShellAuto 123013 (133 over cap) -> 60099 with 62781 margin. gzip+base64 measured first and rejected: bigger win but assumes gzip/base64 on the far host, a new degradation class. Erosion guard extended to all four tiers with a 16KiB margin, proven to fail against the pre-strip baseline. Committed b5ae004a.

title: focus-after-reorder: the dragged tab is not focused when the whole suite runs
description:
## Summary

`focus survives tab reorder > vertical orientation` asserts that the focused
element carries the dragged tab's id before the drag:

    Expected: "4"
    Received: null

`document.activeElement` has no `data-tab-id` at all, so focus is somewhere else
entirely rather than on the wrong tab.

Intermittent, and the intermittency is the finding: in a full container run on
2026-08-07 it PASSED at 17:25 and FAILED at 17:45 from the same tree, at the same
position (31st of 236). Run alone it passes:

    PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh focus-after-reorder   # 2 passed

So it is either a race inside the reorder's focus restoration or a precondition
some earlier spec leaves in the shared stand — the nocx-8rda shape. Not yet
distinguished, and the two need different fixes.

This matters beyond itself: one intermittent test makes a green suite an unusable
gate, because a red run stops meaning anything.

## Steps to Reproduce

    e2e/run-in-container.sh --reporter=list      # repeat; fails in some runs
acceptance_criteria: e2e/focus-after-reorder.spec.ts:155 passes both alone and in a full-suite run, on both browsers, repeatedly. The cause is named as either a focus race inside the reorder or a precondition another spec leaves behind.
close_reason: The spec was racing the app for focus: a new tab's pane focuses its own prompt when the shell's first marker lands (CommandEditor.show -> view.focus), and the test grabbed the tab button before that, so activeElement carried no data-tab-id and the drag never ran. It now waits for the app to finish first. Cause named: a focus race inside the app's own tab-open path, not a precondition left by another spec.

title: AGENTS.md tells you to run a Go gate that cannot pass on a dev box
description:
## Summary

Corrected after finding the answer that already exists — recorded because the
first reading was wrong and the wrongness is the point.

AGENTS.md § Git authority says: "Run the full local gate before pushing, not only
the part you touched: `gofumpt -l .`, `golangci-lint run`, `go test -race ./...`
…". That third command CANNOT pass on a bare dev box. 9 tests in
internal/shellintegration fail for want of `dash` and `zsh`, by design —
nocx-gd84 made the launcher tests fail rather than skip when the shell they exist
to prove is absent, and only ci.yml provisions them.

The working answer is already in the repo and nothing points at it:
`.githooks/containerized-tests.sh`, which the pre-commit hook runs. It builds its
own image (.githooks/images/go-tests) carrying zsh, and — the part that matters —
runs the tests as the HOST user under setpriv rather than as root. That is what
keeps the three read-only-home tests meaningful:

    TestEnsureInstalledRemote_ReadonlyHomeFailsOpenThenConverges
    TestFullLauncher_ReadonlyHome_TransientAndGenerationDash
    TestReadonlyHomeFailsCleanly

Running the same packages in the e2e image, which is root, fails exactly those
three: root ignores the permission bits, so the precondition never holds.

So the defect is not a missing capability. It is that the documented instruction
names the command that cannot work, the one that does work is reachable only as a
side effect of committing, and a session that follows AGENTS.md literally
concludes the repo is broken. This one did, for a while.

## Steps to Reproduce

    go test -count=1 ./internal/shellintegration/   # 9 fail: no dash, no zsh
    grep -n 'go test -race' AGENTS.md               # what you were told to run
acceptance_criteria: AGENTS.md's pre-push gate names a command that actually passes on a developer machine, or says plainly that the hook is the gate and the bare command is not. Whatever it names is verified once on a clean checkout.

title: internal/transport flakes under load — three different tests now, not one
description:
The pre-commit gate failed on TestGitChanged_OverTheWireConformsToContract during a full ./... run in the container, while two other workers were running their own containerised gates on the same machine. Re-run in isolation immediately afterwards: 3/3 green, 1.26s each. The next full gate run passed.

This is the same test nocx-gnf4's sibling investigation already touched: the git.changed notification helper was found to discard id-less notifications when the write goroutine beat the close response, and the follow-up read's timeout poisoned gorilla's readErr. That fix made it 200/200 green at the time.
