Either the fix does not cover this path, or there is a second timing window that only opens under real memory/CPU pressure — which is exactly the condition the earlier tunnel flake needed (concurrent package load, GC, a finalizer closing a socket).

What is NOT in doubt: the product path is not implicated by this evidence alone, and the last investigation of this shape found the defect in the test helper both times. Do not 'fix' the product on this report.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the full containerised gate (go test -race ./...) while other containerised test runs compete for the machine.
2. Observe TestGitChanged_OverTheWireConformsToContract fail after ~5s where it normally takes ~1.3s.

The 5s vs 1.3s gap is the lead: something is waiting out a timeout rather than failing an assertion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The failure is reproduced deliberately — under induced load or an injected delay — rather than waited for. A flake nobody can summon is a flake nobody can prove fixed.
- The root cause names which side owns it: the test helper, the transport, or the notification write path.
- 200 consecutive runs green under the same induced pressure that reproduced it.
- If the product is implicated after all, that is a separate bead with its own evidence — this one is filed on the assumption it is not.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
Second sighting, different test: TestWSServer_OpenPasswordAsk_DoesNotBlockTheReadLoop failed in the full containerised ./... run and passed 3/3 in isolation immediately after (1.03s each). It came from main, not from this branch — so the pattern is the PACKAGE under load, not any one spec.

Three now: the tunnel forwards (nocx-gnf4, root-caused to a GC finalizer closing an unreachable conn's socket), git.changed's contract test, and this one. All three share the shape: green alone, red when the whole module is running -race on a busy machine, and each names a timeout rather than an assertion.

That is worth stating as a hypothesis for whoever takes this: these may not be three bugs. A -race build of this package under CPU contention may simply be slower than the fixed timeouts several of its tests were written against, in which case the fix is a budget the tests agree on rather than three separate repairs. Measure before repairing.

title: Copy the branch name, and open the repository on its hosting
description:
Both asked for by the owner against orca's panel, which puts a copy affordance on the branch and an external-link icon beside the upstream.

The open-in-browser half needs a capability check first: nocx has files.reveal (an OS file-manager reveal, local-only by design attestation, D4) but grep finds no external-URL open anywhere in internal/ or frontend/src. So either that capability exists under a name I did not find, or it has to be added — and if it is added it inherits files.reveal's local-only argument, because opening a URL from an SSH tab's repository is a different question.

The URL itself is derived, not stored: git remote get-url, then a scp-style-to-https conversion (git@github.com:owner/repo.git and https://github.com/owner/repo.git are the same repository, and the panel must not send a user to a URL it invented for a host it does not know).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user copies the current branch name from the panel in one action, and the panel confirms it happened.
- A user opens the repository's hosting page from the panel when the remote is a recognised https/scp-style URL, and the affordance is ABSENT (not disabled) when it is not — design D14: what the panel cannot do, it does not draw.
- A remote that is a local path, or a host with no known web UI, produces no link rather than a guessed one.
- Tests for the URL conversion cover scp-style, https, a trailing .git, a missing .git, and a non-URL remote.
close_reason: Closed

title: two files.spec defects the Expand timeout was hiding
description:
## Summary

Fixing nocx-z9s9.1 let two specs in files.spec.ts reach assertions they had never got to. Neither is a regression — both were unreachable behind the 60s timeout, and both are macOS-only (the container passes all 8).

**1. "show next" counts rows by depth, and macOS has neighbours at that depth.**

    expect(locator(".ui-tree-row[data-depth=\"7\"]")).toHaveCount(50)
    Received: 55 (chromium) / 56 (webkit)

The fixture lives under /var/folders/<x>/<y>/T/, so bigdir sits at depth 7 — and so do the other entries T/ holds on a shared runner (other tests fixtures, nocx-e2e-sshd-* among them). Counting every row at a depth counts strangers. The count belongs to bigdir children, so it should be scoped to that parent rather than to a depth the filesystem chooses.

**2. The clipboard read-back returns empty on Chromium.**

    Expected: "var/folders/.../nocx-files-e2e-aGm2gl/notes.md"
    Received: ""

navigator.clipboard.readText() answers "" with the permissions granted. Worth checking against clipboard.spec.ts, which does the same read-back and passes — the difference between the two is where the answer is.

## Steps to Reproduce

CI only. `PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/files.spec.ts` is green on Linux for both, so this needs the macOS one-spec dispatch loop rather than the container.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The paging count is scoped to the directory it is about, not to a tree depth.
- The clipboard read-back either passes on Chromium or states, from evidence, why this spec cannot do what clipboard.spec.ts does.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
Still open, and worth stating why it will not resolve itself.

The only commit naming this bead (78200bc) is the chore that FILED it, not a fix. Both defects are macOS-only — the container passes all 8 files.spec tests — and since nocx-z9s9.8 moved CI's e2e job to the Linux container, no CI job runs these specs on macOS any more. So this cannot go red again on its own, and it cannot be verified fixed by CI either.

That is a coverage consequence of a decision that was right for other reasons (nocx-z9s9.8 names WKWebView as deliberately out of scope). Flagging it so the next reader does not mistake a green suite for these two being fixed: they are unobserved, not resolved.

title: Which files changed on this branch, not just since the last commit
description:
orca's panel has a COMMITTED ON BRANCH section beside CHANGES: the files this
branch changed relative to its base, with the same +N -N counts. It answers
"what is in my PR", which the working-tree status cannot.

Depends on the counts (nocx-i4ki) for its numbers, and on knowing the base ref.
Filed so it is in the backlog rather than surfacing as another "where is X" —
the owner has now asked that question twice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user on a branch with two commits ahead of its base sees, in the panel, the
  files those commits touched, with line counts, distinct from the working-tree
  lists.
- The base ref is resolved deliberately and the choice is written down: a
  merge-base against the upstream's default branch, or a configured base. This
  is the real design content of this bead and it is NOT decided yet — decide it
  before building, and record it as an ADR if it is not obvious.
- Deliberately out: acting on the section (revert, cherry-pick, open a PR).

title: the e2e container cannot build devharness: git refuses the bind-mounted repo
description:
## Summary

`e2e/run-in-container.sh` died before running a single spec:

    === building devharness ===
    error obtaining VCS status: exit status 128
        Use -buildvcs=false to disable VCS stamping.

The repo is bind-mounted from the host at /work, so its files are owned by the host user while the container runs as root. Git calls that "dubious ownership" and refuses; `go build` stamps VCS info by default, so the devharness build fails.

This matters more than a container papercut: the container is the fast local loop AGENTS.md points at, and while it was broken the only way to learn anything about an e2e failure was a 20-30 minute CI run. That is most of why one bug took three days.

Fix: `git config --global --add safe.directory /work` in e2e/container-entry.sh. Chosen over `-buildvcs=false` so `go build` stays spelled the same here as in headless-run.sh, on CI and on a developer machine — a flag on one path only would have it building something subtly different from everywhere else.

## Steps to Reproduce

    PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/files.spec.ts
    # fails in "building devharness" before playwright starts

## Acceptance Criteria

- `PW_PROJECTS=chromium e2e/run-in-container.sh e2e/files.spec.ts` reaches playwright and reports pass/fail.
close_reason: e2e/run-in-container.sh now reaches playwright; files.spec runs in 10s on chromium and 12s on webkit.

title: files.spec asks WebKit for a clipboard-write permission it does not have
description:
## Summary

`e2e/files.spec.ts:240` calls

    await context.grantPermissions(["clipboard-read", "clipboard-write"])

which throws on WebKit before the test does anything: `browserContext.grantPermissions: Unknown permission: clipboard-write`. One failure per e2e run, webkit only.

The codebase already answers this question. `e2e/clipboard.spec.ts:41` and `:90` carry

    test.skip(({ browserName }) => browserName !== "chromium",
      "clipboard-read permission is Chromium-only; WebKit must be checked manually")

`files.spec` grew the same clipboard dependency without the same guard. Extend the existing answer rather than inventing a second one: the right-click spec gets the same browser guard and the same stated reason.

Read from the trace artifact of run 31164732414 (shard-2, webkit); no re-run was needed to establish it.

## Steps to Reproduce

    gh run download 31164732414 -D traces
    # traces/playwright-traces-shard-2/files-right-clicking-a-row-*/error-context.md

## Acceptance Criteria

- The right-click spec no longer fails on WebKit.
- Whatever guard is used states the reason, as clipboard.spec.ts does — a silent skip would leave the copy path unwatched on the engine the app actually ships in.
close_reason: Confirmed on macOS CI, run 31167919744: 'right-clicking a row offers both copy entries' passes on webkit — the grantPermissions crash is gone and the menu is now watched on the engine the app ships in. The read-back half fails on chromium for an unrelated reason, tracked as nocx-z9s9.5.

title: The merge slot does not serialize two machines: both acquired it, and one defect was fixed twice
description:
On 2026-08-07 two clones of this repo acquired nocx-merge-slot within the same few seconds — 00:21:36 UTC on one machine, essentially simultaneously on the other. Each 'bd merge-slot acquire' consulted its own embedded Dolt database, neither of which had seen the other's claim, and both reported success. Both then merged to main believing they were serialized.

The cost was not theoretical. The same one-line dead export was found and fixed twice, under two beads: 519f2a4 (nocx-d4lh) and the commit for nocx-91ih, which had to be dropped during the rebase. Two people, two investigations, two commits, one defect.

It also left the tracker unable to sync: the two sides had modified the merge-slot row from a common base, and 'bd dolt pull' refused with 'merge conflicts in issues require operator resolution'. In embedded mode there is no 'bd sql' and no 'bd doctor', and 'bd bootstrap' declines when a database already exists, so the only way out was to move .beads/embeddeddolt aside and re-bootstrap from the remote — a manual step no documentation describes.

AGENTS.md already says a claim is not a lock and names a shared sql-server as the real fix, referencing nocx-wj4 (now closed, and about one-way sync rather than this). The gap is that the merge slot is DOCUMENTED as the thing that decides who merges next, and in embedded mode it cannot do that: acquire does not publish, so it cannot observe a remote holder either.

## Steps to Reproduce

On two clones that have not pulled since the other's claim, run 'bd merge-slot acquire' on each. Both succeed and both report themselves as holder. Then run 'bd dolt pull' on either: it refuses with a merge conflict on nocx-merge-slot that neither clone has tooling to resolve in embedded mode.

## Acceptance Criteria

Acquiring the merge slot either observes a claim made on another machine, or fails loudly enough that the caller knows it did not serialize anything. A clone whose issue database has diverged has a documented, supported command to reconcile it — resolving this today required moving the database directory by hand.
notes:
FOUND while landing the git panel epic (nocx-flff); the git work is NOT the cause, it is the load that exposes it.

REPRODUCTION, in the repo's own test container (.githooks/containerized-tests.sh image), on the branch with internal/git present:

  go test -race -count=1 ./internal/git/... ./internal/transport/

fails 2/2 with:
  --- FAIL: TestTunnelTabTeardown_DoesNotStopOtherTabsForward
      ws_tunnel_test.go:320: dial forwarded address 127.0.0.1:PORT: connect: connection refused

Line 320 is the FINAL roundTrip(t, addrB) — so tab B's forward worked, tab A's connection was closed, and B's listener was gone afterwards. That is precisely the invariant the test exists to defend.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, so nobody has to re-derive it:
- baseline (no internal/git), full go test -race ./... in the container: GREEN.
- with internal/git, full ./... in the container: RED, twice, on this test.
- with internal/git, ./internal/transport/ ALONE: green (5+ runs).
- with internal/git, transport + git/spawn only: green. transport + git/local only: green.
- with internal/git, transport + ALL THREE git packages: RED, twice.
- baseline, transport + shellintegration (another heavy process-spawning package): green.
- the tunnel test alone under artificial CPU load on baseline: green (3 runs).

So it is not CPU load and not one package; it is the degree of concurrent package execution. The git work adds three packages to the parallel set and tips a window that already existed.

WHERE TO LOOK: unregisterConn -> stopOwnerTunnels (ws.go:3009). The design is tab-scoped and the comment says each forward holds its own pooled reference; under concurrency B's forward is being stopped anyway, or its listener is closed by A's teardown path. Both tunnels in the test use profileId ssh:p1:1, i.e. they share one connection, which is the case the invariant is about.

This blocks nothing structurally but it turns the pre-commit gate red for any change that adds parallel test packages.

title: The transport's dispatch knows all 86 methods; replace the switch with a registry
description:
handleControlFrame (internal/transport/ws.go:982) is one switch over 86 method names reaching 44 handler entry points, in a 3000-line file. The transport therefore knows the whole product's vocabulary: adding vault.createSecret means editing the WebSocket layer. That is AD-8 the wrong way round — the module that owns a behaviour should declare it, at the composition root.

Shape agreed with the owner and reviewed twice: a registry keyed on EXACT method names (not namespace prefixes — a prefix router leaves a second switch inside each family and reports collisions weakly). Each module registers its handlers and its execution class. The transport keeps envelope validation, correlation, routing, admission bounds and cancellation, and nothing else.

Namespace-keyed ORDERING was considered and rejected: invariants cross namespaces (export.import mutates profiles, groups, settings and secrets in one call; open crosses session, profile resolution, vault and sshConfig), so per-namespace FIFO is an attractive false guarantee. See nocx-u687 for the ordering contract itself.

Depends on nocx-u687: that bead introduces the bounded executor and the execution classes this registry consumes, so doing them in the other order writes the same 86 lines twice.

## Acceptance Criteria

internal/transport contains no switch over product method names. Adding a method to an existing module requires no edit under internal/transport. A duplicate registration is refused at startup rather than silently shadowed.
notes: 2026-08-08: the executor contract this bead consumes is nocx-sfv6.3 (internal/transport/control). It schedules declared work and never learns a method name, so this registry supplies handler + lane + conflict declaration without the executor needing rework.

title: lint fixture gate feeds JSON through echo, which /bin/sh mangles
description:
frontend/lint-fixtures/gate.sh captures `eslint --format json` into a variable and pipes
it to node with `echo "$eslint_json"`. /bin/sh's echo expands backslash escapes (macOS
ships bash with xpg_echo on for /bin/sh; dash does the same on Linux), so every \n inside
the JSON's `source` field becomes a real newline and JSON.parse fails:

    PARSE FAIL: Bad control character in string literal in JSON at position 1573

The inline node scripts answer that with `process.exit(2)`, and `set -eu` turns the
failed assignment into an exit — so the gate dies at gate.sh:213 having printed only the
kit-identity line, with no message of its own. From the hook it reads as
"FAIL: solid negative fixture gate", which names the wrong thing entirely.

Not caught before because nothing ran it: the gate is hook-only (`npm run lint` does not
include lint:fixture-check, so CI's frontend job never invokes it) and .githooks was not
installed in this clone until nocx-mz9d.

## Steps to Reproduce

    cd frontend && sh ./lint-fixtures/gate.sh; echo $?
    # prints the kit-identity OK line, then exits 2 with no explanation

## Acceptance Criteria

- `sh ./lint-fixtures/gate.sh` reaches its own final line and exits 0.
- JSON payloads are piped with printf '%s', not echo, wherever the gate round-trips them
  through a shell variable.
- A gate that dies mid-way says which check died; exit 2 with no message is what made
  this read as a solid-plugin failure.
close_reason: Closed

title: deadcode baseline is per-OS in one direction only, so the first macOS run reports a NEW violation
description:
.githooks/deadcode-baseline.json documents that build-tag-gated entries "only appear on
the OS they build for, so an entry that vanishes on another platform is a free shrink,
not a violation". Only that direction was handled. The twin the *other* OS compiles is a
different file path, so it is reported as a NEW violation and fails the hook.

Concretely: the baseline lists internal/vault/system/secretservice_linux.go
SecretServiceAvailable (and secretServiceAvailableVia). On macOS those two vanish — the
free shrink the note describes — and secretservice_other.go SecretServiceAvailable
appears instead, which nothing had listed. Neither half has a production caller on
either OS; both are reached only from integration_test.go.

Found the first time .githooks/pre-commit ran on macOS in this clone (core.hooksPath was
unset until nocx-mz9d), where it blocked an unrelated commit.

Same shape as nocx-koki: a gate artifact produced in one environment and checked in
another. update-deadcode-baseline.mjs cannot fix it by itself — it sees one OS at a
time, so the half it did not compile looks like a shrink and it removes it.

## Steps to Reproduce

On macOS, with the hook installed:

    node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs
    # DEADCODE RATCHET: ... 1 NEW:
    #   NEW: internal/vault/system/secretservice_other.go: SecretServiceAvailable

## Acceptance Criteria

- The baseline holds both halves of every build-tag-gated pair, and says so in its
  header note.
- `node .githooks/check-deadcode.mjs` passes on macOS and on Linux without either run
  editing the baseline.
- update-deadcode-baseline.mjs does not silently drop the half it did not compile (or,
  if it still would, the header says the file must be hand-merged and why).
close_reason: Closed

title: the local Go gate runs only Linux, but the product is macOS-first
description:
.githooks/pre-commit:154 runs `go test -race` in the Linux container
(.githooks/containerized-tests.sh). The shipped product is macOS-first (ci.yml's own
runner decision says so: darwin is the target, and internal/pty's PTY semantics are only
meaningful there). The container is therefore structurally blind to every defect that
lives in the difference between the two filesystems.

nocx-koki is three such defects at once, shipped on the same day: a symlinked TMPDIR
(/var -> /private/var), a case-insensitive APFS, and a fake whose two halves only agree
on Linux. All three were green in the container and red on CI's macOS job.

The container is still the right default — it is ~15x faster and it keeps the keychain
out of the loop (nocx-o4hg). The question is what the gate does *in addition*, not what
it does instead.

## Steps to Reproduce

    grep -n 'containerized' .githooks/pre-commit
    go test -count=1 ./internal/filesystem/...   # red on macOS, green in the container

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Go change staged on macOS cannot reach main with a macOS-only test failure.
- Whatever the mechanism (host run for the touched packages, a pre-push host gate, or
  CI on push), the cost is stated in seconds and measured, not assumed.
- The container stays the default for the slow path; this does not undo nocx-o4hg.

title: Discard changes from the Git panel, with a confirmation that names what is destroyed
acceptance_criteria: A file's changes can be discarded from the panel behind a confirmation. It handles three cases the panel must not conflate: an untracked file (discard means DELETE FROM DISK), a tracked modification (restore), and a partially staged file. This is the only action in the panel that destroys work with no undo.

title: The Git panel works on an SSH tab, over the relay
acceptance_criteria: On an SSH tab the Git panel shows that host's repository and its mutation controls are present and work. Requires an operation channel the relay does not have: named request/response for open,status,diff,stage,unstage,stageAll,unstageAll,commit,headMessage, plus cancellation, results bounded on the machine doing the work, and the domain outcomes of the design's 5.1. NOT stdin, separated stderr or an exit status - that is the process-shaped seam the design rejected (D16), and asking the relay for it would reintroduce it through the backlog. The reserved metadata msg-type is a one-way feed, so this is a protocol decision before it is a coding task.

title: frontend: the unified diff tab on the extracted host
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a row opens a read-only tab whose singletonKey is git:toplevel:side:path, so one row is one tab and staged vs unstaged are two; + lines, - lines and hunk headers are decorated; binary, tooLarge, empty and gone each render as themselves; the tab is a snapshot that offers Reload and never re-reads underneath the reader.
close_reason: Diff tab on the extracted ReadOnlyHost: singletonKey per {toplevel,side,path}, frozen origin, five wire states, D7 snapshot-plus-Reload. 28 tests. Landed 6aa907b.

title: frontend: the Git panel and its view descriptor, wired into the activity bar
acceptance_criteria: A Git view appears in the activity bar after Files and Ports; the header shows branch, upstream and ahead/behind; Staged and Unstaged render FileStatusRow rows; stage, unstage, stage-all, unstage-all and the commit form with Amend are present and enabled from the state a user starts in; on an SSH tab the mutation controls are absent from the DOM, not disabled.
close_reason: Delivered with nocx-es2y — the panel and its view descriptor landed together with the store in 6aa907b.

title: file-viewer: extract a read-only CodeMirror host to the ownership contract
acceptance_criteria: A host module owns EditorView construction, read-only enforcement, base theme, setDoc, focus() and dispose(); FileViewerContent uses it and its existing tests are green unchanged; the host has its own tests for read-only enforcement and disposal; callers append their own extensions and the host never inspects them; tsc passes.
close_reason: Read-only CM6 host extracted to frontend/src/read-only-host.ts per the ownership contract; viewer refactored onto it with its tests unmodified and green; read-only enforcement verified against CM6's own facet combine (values[0] wins). Landed ffa43a0.

title: ui kit: CollectionRow gains typed activation and density; FileStatusRow owns the status vocabulary
acceptance_criteria: CollectionRow accepts onActivate plus keyboard semantics and a density variant as a typed data-*, and Connections and Credentials are unchanged by default; FileStatusRow composes it and owns the M/A/D/R/C/U/? glyph-and-tone table; both have a CSS file, a stable identity class, tests and a README row; npm test and tsc pass.
close_reason: CollectionRow gained typed activation + density (existing callers opt-in, unchanged); FileStatusRow owns the seven-letter glyph-and-tone table. Coordinator corrections: removed a wrapper div that orphaned role=listitem from role=list (test added), un-exported FileStatusTone per the ratchet. Landed 2820faf.

title: TrustHostKey leaves a matching wildcard known_hosts entry in place
description:
TrustHostKey compares known_hosts hostnames literally, while golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/knownhosts applies * and ? wildcard matching when it verifies. So accepting a changed key for db.example.com appends the new key but leaves a line like '*.example.com ssh-ed25519 <old-key>' untouched — and that line still matches db.example.com. The key the user just rejected goes on being valid for that host.

This predates the route-specific jump-host work (nocx-shat) and is independent of it: opaque jump-route identities cannot match a wildcard pattern, so only the direct route is affected.

Found while splitting PR #64 — it was recorded in an untracked _bmad-output/deferred-work.md, which is not a place work survives.

## Steps to Reproduce

Put a wildcard line in known_hosts covering a host: '*.example.com ssh-ed25519 AAAA<old>'. Connect to db.example.com, which now presents a different key. Accept the change through the host-key dialog. Inspect known_hosts: both the wildcard line and the new specific line are present, and a verification against the old key still succeeds.

## Where to look

internal/ssh/ssh_real.go, around the known_hosts name comparison in the trust write (roughly lines 490-506 at the time of writing).

## Acceptance Criteria

Accepting a changed key removes every known_hosts entry that would still verify the rejected key for that host, wildcard patterns included, before appending the accepted one. A test puts a matching wildcard line in known_hosts, accepts a changed key, and asserts the old key no longer verifies.
close_reason: Fixed by deleting our matcher, not extending it: knownhosts is now asked which lines cover a host. Wildcards narrowed with a negation, single-host lines removed, all algorithms revoked, @revoked and @cert-authority preserved, postcondition validated before rename, unparseable files refused. 9030eb7

title: Control-frame handlers block the readLoop while they do I/O
description:
handleControlFrame dispatches most methods synchronously on the readLoop — the one goroutine that also feeds every session's input on that WebSocket. Several of them block for a long time: connections.test runs a 30s SSH probe, dialog.openFile waits on a native dialog until the user answers (indefinite), sshConfig.aliases shells out to ssh -G with a 10s timeout per pattern, and the vault methods can wait on a cold keychain. While any of those runs, no tab on that connection can send a keystroke.

## Steps to Reproduce

Open two tabs on one backend. In the connection manager, press Test on a host that does not answer (so the 30s probe runs to its timeout). Type in the other tab. Nothing arrives until the probe returns.

## Why this is filed separately

PR #64 fixed it by putting ~20 handler families behind 'go s.handleXxx(...)'. That was dropped when the PR was split (see nocx-o2le), because it is a bigger decision than it looks:

- It removes the ordering guarantee the control plane has always had. Today a renderer can send profiles.create then profiles.list and rely on the second seeing the first. Concurrent dispatch breaks that, and nothing in the renderer or the tests says which methods depend on it.
- It spawns a goroutine per control frame with no bound.
- The stores are mutex-guarded, so this is not a data race — it is a semantics change, and it needs an ADR plus tests pinning which sequences must stay ordered.

## Where to look

internal/transport/ws.go, handleControlFrame. 'open' is already dispatched with 'go' on main, so the precedent exists — but it is a method with no ordering dependents.

## Acceptance Criteria

A long-running control method no longer stalls input on other sessions, proven by a test over the real socket. A create-then-read sequence from one connection still observes its own write. The ordering decision is recorded as an ADR.
notes:
Design consultation done (2026-08-06), not started. Decisions reached, to be confirmed with the owner before code:
- Two execution classes, not three: ingress-critical (ack + vault.unlockResolved + connections.passwordResolved, strictly non-blocking) and bounded async (everything else). The two resolvers must never queue: RequestUnlock/RequestConnectionPassword block on a channel until the matching *Resolved arrives on the SAME socket.
- NO implicit ordering. Verified: nothing in the renderer depends on it. Every mutation is awaited before the dependent read (connections.tsx:1643-1663 is canonical); no unawaited-mutation-then-read pattern exists anywhere. The ADR declares the absence and the acceptance test must await the mutation response before the read, or it canonises FIFO by accident.
- Per-namespace ordering was considered and REJECTED: invariants cross namespaces (export.import mutates profiles+groups+settings+secrets in one call; open crosses session/profile/vault/sshConfig), so a namespace FIFO is an attractive false guarantee.
- Registry keyed on EXACT methods (not prefixes) replacing the 86-case switch is the right end state but is separate scope - see the follow-up bead. The executor contract this bead introduces is what that registry later consumes, so it is not throwaway.
- BLOCKER, must be in this bead: 43 context.Background() calls in internal/transport. Cancellation stops at the transport boundary. Invisible today because the readLoop blocks anyway; after this fix every detached handler outlives its connection. Propagating the connection context is part of the fix, not a follow-up.
- Also fix: ws_probe.go:164 runs the 30s probe on context.Background().
- Ordering is per-connection in any case (s.conns is a set; asks broadcast to all). The ADR must say two connections have no ordering relationship - nowhere written today.
2026-08-08: triaged as structural. This is now the epic nocx-sfv6, which carries a discovered-from edge back here; u687 is blocked by it and closes when the epic delivers. The design consultation that produced the epic read the code and overturned two of the six decisions recorded above: (a) 'ingress-critical runs inline and strictly non-blocking' is unachievable while resolvers answer through writeJSON, which holds wsConn.mu for up to 10s (ws.go:744-755) — the interval must end at the channel signal, needing a bounded outbound queue (nocx-sfv6.1); (b) 'no ordering at all' is too broad — it says nothing about two connections, and resize/close are sent unawaited by the renderer (ipc.ts:467-484) while handleResize blocks on a dead SSH link (ws.go:1509), so they are ordering-sensitive AND blocking (nocx-sfv6.6). The 59-context.Background sweep is narrowed: pumpToRing (ws.go:1410) keeps Background on purpose for AD-9 replay (nocx-sfv6.7).
close_reason: Superseded, not fixed. Triage turned it structural: the fix is the epic nocx-sfv6, which carries the discovered-from edge back here and delivers the same acceptance (a long control method no longer stalls input on other sessions, proven over the real socket). Closed rather than left open because a task cannot be blocked by an epic, so it would otherwise sit in bd ready as a second front for one piece of work. The design notes on this bead are superseded by the epic's — two of their six decisions were overturned; see the appended note.

title: Step 9: spec-review gate offers stress-test
close_reason: Owner chose an external codex review instead of the stress-test gate.

title: Step 7: spec self-review
close_reason: Self-review found two inconsistencies (method count; Amend prefill had no wire method) — both fixed before commit.

title: vault.spec 'no keyring, full round trip' flakes on webkit under a full-suite run
description:
## Summary

In a local both-browser run of the seven headless specs (20 tests, one worker), [webkit] vault.spec.ts:92 failed waiting 10s for .ui-vault-code-block-wrap .ui-code-block — the recovery code shown after Set Up. Re-running e2e/vault.spec.ts alone on webkit passed twice in 6.5s each.

So it is load- or order-dependent, not a defect in the flow. The 10s budget is the suspect: webkit is the slower engine here and the vault Set Up does real key derivation.

Filed rather than fixed because a timeout raised without evidence is how a real failure gets hidden. Wanted first: whether it reproduces in CI now that e2e-headless runs these specs, and whether it is always this assertion.

## Steps to Reproduce

e2e/headless-run.sh with all seven spec files, both browsers: 17 passed, 1 failed. Same spec alone on webkit: 2 passed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Either a named cause, or evidence that the wait is genuinely too short for webkit under load and a budget sized from measurement.
- Not 'bumped the timeout until it stopped failing'.

title: the root eslint config is never run by CI
description:
## Summary

frontend/ is linted by the frontend job. The repository root has its own flat config (eslint.config.mjs) covering e2e/, playwright.config.ts and the scripts, and nothing in ci.yml ever invokes it — the closest step, 'Typecheck the e2e suite', runs npm ci and npm run typecheck only.

Found by running it by hand while fixing nocx-w4vy: four errors, all pre-existing, none of them caused by that change. Two unused constants in connection-password.spec.ts (TAB, INPUT), one in quick-connect.spec.ts (QUICK_CONNECT_LIST), and a no-useless-escape in nocxify-journey.spec.ts:199.

Small findings, but they are evidence the gate has never fired. Same family as nocx-hzfe: a check that exists and is not wired is indistinguishable from one that passes.

Deliberately not fixed inside the nocx-w4vy commit — wiring the gate while a release branch is red would have mixed an unrelated cleanup into a change that needed to be readable.

## Steps to Reproduce

npx eslint e2e/ playwright.config.ts from the repository root: 4 errors. grep ci.yml for eslint: only the frontend job's npm run lint, which is scoped to frontend/.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The four existing errors are fixed.
- ci.yml runs the root eslint, in the job that already installs the root dependencies.
- Introducing a lint error under e2e/ turns CI red.

title: backend-linux matrix cancels the variant that would have said which keyring case broke
description:
## Summary

ci.yml's backend-linux runs with-keyring: [true, false] to compare two platform behaviours. The matrix had no fail-fast: false, so the first variant to fail cancelled the other — destroying exactly the comparison the job exists to make. The e2e matrix already sets it; this one was missed.

Noticed while reading the wails crossplatform-build guide the owner supplied, which makes the same point for platform builds ('Failure in one platform build won't impact the others').

Not a defect in the product and not the cause of any current red run — a diagnosis-quality gap, filed so the change is not a silent drive-by.

## Acceptance Criteria

- backend-linux carries fail-fast: false and both variants report independently.
close_reason: Closed

title: Completing into an empty folder says No matches, blaming the user for the folder
description:
## Summary

Accepting a directory candidate re-queries into it with open intent — the owner"s "Tab jumps to the next folder" (controller.apply). When the folder holds nothing, the panel that opens says "No matches", which reads as if the completion had failed at the exact moment it succeeded. Nothing was typed for anything to fail to match.

The vocabulary already distinguishes these: dirs-only-empty explains a folder that holds files when the command takes directories. A folder that holds nothing needed the same treatment.

## Steps to Reproduce

In a directory holding `alpha/` (empty) and `beta/`, type `cd al` and press Tab.
The line completes to `cd alpha/` — correct — and the panel opens on alpha/ saying
"No matches".

## Fix

A new EmptyReason, empty-dir, chosen on the fs provider by whether the user typed a
prefix at all: a token that is empty or ends in `/` is a listing, so an empty answer
means the folder is empty; a token with a last segment is a prefix, and an empty
answer there really is no-match.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Completing into an empty folder names the folder as empty, not "No matches".
- A prefix that matches nothing still says "No matches".
- Both are covered by unit tests on the provider, and the e2e acceptance spec asserts
  the message a user sees after accepting a directory.
close_reason: Fixed by b4de24a — accepting a directory candidate re-queries into it, and an empty folder now reads as empty instead of 'No matches'. Not gate-covered (UI), so verified by reading the commit rather than by a green suite.

title: Does a hand-typed ssh to a non-integrated host leave Files showing the local machine?
description: Design §0: "the panel shows files of the machine you are currently in, andnever of another one." A hand-typed `ssh` to a host with NO shell integrationmay defeat that: the backend session is still the local one, so the panel goeson serving local files while the prompt is on the remote host.terminal-content.ts:461 intends to prevent it by returning no origin inside adetected environment, but the entered transition is deliberately withhelduntil the passport/marker sequence succeeds (terminal-content.ts:989, :1314) —and a host with no integration may never produce it. So the safety claim andthe transition timing may not agree. Raised by codex; NOT yet reproduced, andnocx-mlm7 landed hand-typed-ssh adoption since — the first job is to find outwhether the hole is real on a host that never adopts.## Steps to Reproduce1. In a local tab, hand-type `ssh` to a host with no shell integration and   which never adopts.2. Look at the Files panel: does it still list the LOCAL filesystem?## Acceptance Criteria- Either a test shows the origin goes unavailable when a shell changes  machines without integration, or the panel says plainly that it represents  the managed session and not necessarily the visible prompt.- Whichever it is, it is asserted, not assumed.

title: TestPasswordRequest_* flakes at its 2s deadline under a loaded full -race run
description: The TestPasswordRequest_* family in internal/transport fails intermittentlyunder the full `go test -race ./...` run, never in isolation. Three differentmembers have been seen failing (_Cancelled, _SubmittedUseOnce,_ContextCancelled), each at exactly 2.00s — so the suspect is a shared 2sdeadline that is tight rather than a defect in any one test.## Steps to Reproduce1. `go test -race ./...` on a loaded machine (e.g. with several agent workers   running). One TestPasswordRequest_* fails at 2.00s.2. `go test -race ./internal/transport/ -run TestPasswordRequest -count=3`   passes every time.## Acceptance Criteria- The deadline is derived from a named constant with headroom, or the wait is  event-driven rather than timed.- `go test -race ./...` run under artificial load 10x shows no failure in this  family.
close_reason: Duplicate of nocx-yht3, fixed on release/v0.1.0 (dcb6512) and merged in at 331974d: the 2s deadline is named wantWithin and raised to 30s

title: The e2e home boundary does not cover the login keychain
description:
## Summary

internal/app/app.go:275 probes the system vault provider on every backend start, and the comment there says what it is: "a probe is a real keychain write". e2e/home-isolation.ts redirects $HOME and names the three things that covers — ~/.config/nocx-dev, ~/.nocx plus rc files, ~/.ssh/config. The login keychain is a fourth, and $HOME does not move it: go-keyring talks to the Keychain service, not to a directory.

`wails dev` rebuilds and re-signs the binary each run, so macOS re-asks for access every time, and a suite that restarts the backend per spec asks continuously. The owner saw a keychain prompt every two seconds while an e2e run was in progress on his own machine.

This is the same class as nocx-ti8w: correct-looking isolation that does not cover everything a backend reaches.

## Steps to Reproduce

On macOS, `npx playwright test` (default `wails dev` path). Keychain access dialogs
appear repeatedly for the duration of the run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A local e2e run touches no real keychain. Either the boundary covers the keystore
  the way it covers $HOME, or the documented local path runs somewhere that has no
  keychain to reach.
- The boundary documents the keystore explicitly, so the next reader does not have
  to rediscover that $HOME does not move it.

title: Four e2e tests pinned the activity-bar registry, so shipping Ports turned them red
description:
## Summary

sidebar.spec.ts (3 tests) and proof-matrix.spec.ts (Focus matrix > Button, Roving tabindex > Home/End) assert "exactly one action button, zero view buttons, the gear carries tabindex=0". That was the census on 2026-07-28 when they were written. b26bb62 (2026-08-04, nocx-wzc4.7) registered Ports as a view, which is a feature working as intended — and roving tabindex moved tabindex=0 onto the Ports button. The product is right; the tests pinned a census instead of a rule.

Note ArrowDown/ArrowUp in the activity bar does not fail — it now silently test.skip()s, because it looks for the gear by tabbing and Tab lands on Ports. A rotted test that skips is worse than one that fails.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run 31095239709 e2e shards 1-3, both browsers: sidebar.spec.ts:16/32/40 and
proof-matrix.spec.ts:64/707 fail with counts and tabindex mismatches.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The tests assert rules that survive the next view being registered: the zone
  partition (data-view in Views, data-action in Actions), the roving-tabindex
  invariant, and the collapse-follows-active-view rule.
- No test hard-codes how many views are registered.
- The ArrowDown/ArrowUp test asserts movement rather than skipping.
close_reason: Fix is on main and the gate that would catch a regression is green on ec3e2a7 (run 31246707047: backend, backend-linux x2, frontend, e2e all pass). Fixed by 03d9517 (the activity bar tests assert its rules, not its census) and e187a34.

title: File viewer: lazy-load CodeMirror language modes — 140.7 KB gzip on every launch today
description:
frontend/src/file-viewer/language-registry.ts statically imports eight
@codemirror/lang-* packages. Measured by the worker that built it: +373.6 KB raw
/ +140.7 KB gzip, of which ~13 KB gzip is the fixed highlight core and the rest
is the language set.

That is paid on every launch by every user, including those who never open a
file — the panel is optional and the viewer is a subset of it.

Why this matters more here than the number alone suggests: this repository
REJECTED Kobalte in July over ~34 KB gzip of shared core, in
.internal/specs/2026-07-27-kobalte-spike-report.md, against the 25-35 KB total
budget of ADR-0012. Shipping 140 KB of language modes while that rejection
stands is an inconsistency somebody will reasonably point at.

CodeMirror supports this cleanly: a Compartment plus a StateEffect reconfigure,
with the LanguageSupport resolved by dynamic import when a file of that type is
actually opened. The registry already maps extension to language, so the change
is to make its values thunks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Opening the app loads none of the eight language packages; opening a .json
  file loads exactly one.
- The measured gzip delta of the base bundle drops to the highlight core alone.
  Report the number before and after — the claim is a measurement, not an
  assertion.
- The viewer's 24 tests stay green, including that a file whose language is
  still loading renders as plain text rather than empty.
acceptance_criteria: The base bundle loads no language package; opening a file loads exactly the one it needs; the gzip delta is measured before and after; the viewer's tests stay green including the still-loading case.

title: Files panel: automatic refresh — fsnotify locally, polling over SFTP, degraded mode visible
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-06-file-manager-design.md §5.5 and D5. Everything
below it is built and shipped in nocx-708q; this is the wave that makes the tree
update by itself.

WHY IT IS NOT OSC 133. The superseded draft refreshed on command-end, claiming
"command-end is precisely when an agent has finished writing". That is false and
this repo says so at frontend/src/agent-status.ts:3 — an agent runs as ONE long
shell command, so OSC 133 cannot see inside it and the tree would never refresh
during exactly the session the panel exists for. The owner then rejected keying
on agent activity at all, correctly: a file can be created or changed by anyone,
including cron, another session and another person. So refresh comes from the
filesystem.

WHAT EXISTS ALREADY:
- Provider.Watch is in the contract; local and sftp both return a typed
  ErrWatchUnavailable today, deliberately, rather than a channel that never
  fires — a silent non-degrade is what the design forbids.
- Binding.swapWatches implements the atomic replace-set semantics with tests.
- files.watch and files.changed exist on the wire with schemas and Go
  conformance tests. The transport already resolves the notification's
  destination at emit time from the session's current subscriber and coalesces
  a dirty-path set while no subscriber is attached.
- The renderer does NOT subscribe yet; src/generated/files.{watch,changed}.ts
  are baselined dead exports precisely because of that, with a note saying they
  should be deleted if this wave never happens.

WHAT THIS BEAD ADDS:
- Local: fsnotify (NEW dependency, needs go.mod), one non-recursive watch per
  EXPANDED directory. Events are invalidation hints, never the diff: coalesce,
  re-list, compare Rev. Re-establish on rename/delete/recreate/overflow. Ceiling
  on watched directories and outstanding re-lists.
- Remote: polling. SFTP has no change notification in the protocol; the
  asymmetry is honest, not a gap to close cleverly. Jittered interval, per-host
  concurrency limit, exponential slow-down on failure, paused while the panel is
  hidden, one immediate poll on becoming visible. A directory that hit the entry
  cap is NOT polled — it would re-enumerate every tick to compute a digest it
  will refuse.
- The renderer subscribes to files.changed and re-lists.

DEGRADATION IS A BADGE, NOT A BANNER (§5.5, three levels):
- Remote polling is the designed mode and warns about nothing. A permanent
  banner over a feature that IS working is how the admission stops being read.
- A local watch that could not be established falls back to polling and shows a
  persistent "Polling" warning badge beside Refresh, detail on hover, cleared
  the instant watching recovers. The transition still gets its toast; the badge
  is what answers "why is this stale?" ten minutes later.
- Refresh that has actually STOPPED escalates to a sticky banner with Retry,
  because that is materially worse than degraded-but-working.

REJECTED, AND THEY STAY REJECTED: a shell hook emitting changes observes only
what passes through that shell — not the agent, not cron, not another person —
while the product claims automatic refresh; a partial observer sold as a
complete one is worse than polling. inotifywait/fswatch assume software on the
host. The Tier-B remote helper (architecture.md:203 names "richer remote
metadata (file-tree)" as its revisit trigger) is a LATER epic, consent-gated,
that must augment polling and degrade back to it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Writing to a file from outside nocx makes its row update with nobody pressing
  anything — the one clause of design §7's end-to-end assertion that nocx-708q
  could not meet. Asserted in e2e, locally.
- A local watch that cannot be established shows the polling badge for as long
  as it is true, and clears it when watching recovers. Asserted, not inspected.
- A capped directory is never polled.
- src/generated/files.watch.ts and files.changed.ts leave the dead-export
  baseline.
acceptance_criteria: A file changed from outside nocx updates its row with no user action; a failed local watch shows a persistent polling badge that clears on recovery; a capped directory is never polled; the two generated wire types leave the dead-export baseline.
notes:
LANDED EARLY, inside nocx-708q, in 95761b7 and 6d98b2e — the owner had named automatic refresh
as first-slice scope and deferring it here was the coordinator's error, not his.

What shipped: the panel subscribes to files.changed, maintains the watch set against what is
expanded (files.watch REPLACES the set, so collapsing cannot leak a watch), re-lists on
invalidation while preserving expansion state, and skips the re-list when the notification's rev
matches what is already applied. Remote polling shows nothing because it is the designed mode
there; a local binding that could not establish live watching shows a persistent Polling badge;
refresh that has actually stopped escalates to a sticky Retry.

Also fixed here: the watch baseline was taken on the first poll tick, 500 ms after files.watch
returned, so a change inside that window was folded into the baseline and never announced. The
inotify rule the comment invoked is right; inotify installs synchronously and this did not. The
baseline is now taken inside the handler, proven red-then-green, and the e2e's 600 ms wait — which
had been hiding it — is gone. Design §7's last clause, 'writing to the file from outside nocx
makes the row update without anyone pressing anything', is now met and asserted headlessly.

WHAT REMAINS FOR THIS BEAD, and it is the original point of it: the change signal is a
TRANSPORT-SIDE digest poll at 500 ms for BOTH providers. That is honest and it works, but it is
not what §5.5 specifies:
  - Local should use fsnotify (a new go.mod dependency), one non-recursive watch per expanded
    directory, events treated as invalidation hints rather than as the diff, re-established on
    rename/delete/recreate/overflow, with a ceiling on watched directories.
  - Remote polling should gain jitter, a per-host concurrency limit, exponential slow-down on
    repeated failure, and it must not poll a directory that hit the entry cap — today a capped
    directory is re-enumerated every tick to compute a digest it will refuse.
  - Provider.Watch still returns ErrWatchUnavailable in both providers; the provider-side seam
    exists and is unimplemented.
So the user-visible feature is delivered and the mechanism underneath is the placeholder.

title: Ten 2-second wall-clock deadlines in password_requester_test flake under load
description:
TestPasswordRequest_SubmittedWithRemember failed the container pre-commit gate on 'read notification: read tcp ...: i/o timeout' after exactly 2.00s. password_requester_test.go carries ten hardcoded 2-second deadlines (SetReadDeadline and time.After). Unlike nocx-zlvw, where the event never happened at all, here it does arrive and merely arrives late — the case that bead's acceptance describes as the other branch: derive the deadline from a stated budget rather than pick a number. A timing-sensitive assertion that only fails in company is what erodes trust in the gate.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run the internal/transport suite with the CPU saturated:

    for i in $(seq 1 12); do while :; do :; done & done
    go test -race -count=20 -run TestPasswordRequest ./internal/transport/

Occasionally internal/transport fails at password_requester_test.go:146.
acceptance_criteria: The deadlines in internal/transport/password_requester_test.go are derived from a stated budget with the reason written down, generous enough that what fails is a notification that never arrives rather than a machine that was busy. The file passes under -count=20 with the CPU saturated.
close_reason: Fix is on main and the gate that would catch a regression is green on ec3e2a7 (run 31246707047: backend, backend-linux x2, frontend, e2e all pass). Fixed by dcb6512 and 53df4f1 — the contract waits use the deadline the package already agreed on.

title: Full frontend gate misreads multi-class shell tokens
description:
The containerized full Vitest gate consistently fails editor.test.ts:710 while the same file passes alone. The assertion indexes span.className as one key, so a valid token carrying multiple semantic classes is invisible under tok-command.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run the repository pre-commit hook or the full containerized frontend test gate. Observe editor.test.ts:710 fail with tok-command undefined; run editor.test.ts alone and observe it pass.
acceptance_criteria: The shell syntax highlighting assertion evaluates each CSS class on a token independently, and the full frontend pre-commit gate passes.
notes: Reopened 2026-08-06: closed while the work was still only on PR #64, which is not merged. #64 was split into per-concern branches; this bead's work lives on one of them and is not on main yet.
close_reason: Merged to main while splitting PR #64 into per-concern branches.

title: TestTunnelConn_DialAfterCloseFails: Done did not close, on the linux runner
description: ssh_tunnel_test.go:316 fails on ubuntu-latest in run 31083388224 after 5.03s - the Done channel never closed inside the test's wait. Passes locally with -race in 1s. Shape of a timing assumption that holds on a fast machine and not on a loaded runner, but that is a hypothesis: it may equally be a close path that genuinely leaks when a dial is in flight.
acceptance_criteria: The cause is named rather than assumed, and the test passes on the backend-linux job across repeated runs.
close_reason: Duplicate of nocx-zlvw, which was filed 2026-08-05 with a better diagnosis: the same ssh_tunnel_test.go:316 'Done did not close', already traced to a 5-second wall-clock deadline that only misses when the machine is loaded. Filed without running the 'already filed?' check first — bd query 'status=open' did not return it, and the title search that would have (bd list --status all) was not run.

title: nativeports does not see a port the test itself opened, on the macOS runner
description: TestProvider_ListsPortOpenedByThisTest fails on macos-latest in run 31083388224: 'provider did not list the port this test opened (49225) - stale table or missing listener'. Passes locally on linux with -race. The provider is per-OS, so this is either the macOS implementation or a permission the runner withholds. Whichever it is, the product ships this provider on macOS, so a runner that cannot exercise it is a gap in the gate as much as a bug.
acceptance_criteria: The cause is named. Either the macOS provider is fixed and the test passes, or the test states in the product-visible way why the capability is unavailable - never a silent skip.
close_reason: Fix is on main and the gate that would catch a regression is green on ec3e2a7 (run 31246707047: backend, backend-linux x2, frontend, e2e all pass). Fixed by 87ae6e6, 66558a7 and d8e15d4 — an lsof row ends in its state, not its address.

title: Remote path completion returns an empty list on the macOS runner
description: TestSSHCompleter_E2E_RemotePaths fails on macos-latest in run 31083388224: 'remote /etc completion: passwd not found in []' - the completer returned no candidates at all rather than the wrong ones. Passes locally on linux with -race. The test drives the in-repo sshd from cmd/e2e-sshd, so the question is what that sshd's shell resolves on a macOS runner. Not yet diagnosed.
acceptance_criteria: The cause is named and the test passes on the macOS backend job.
close_reason: The remote completion script used declare -A (bash 4.0+); macOS ships 3.2, where it aborts the script and the remote returns nothing — so remote path completion was empty against every stock-macOS host. Replaced with a delimited-string dedup whose membership test quotes the entry, plus a static check for bash-4-only constructs so the Linux job cannot hide the next one.

title: Burn down the dead-code baseline: 86 unreachable Go funcs and the frontend's unused exports
description:
The ratchet in nocx-ckoy.1 stops the pile GROWING. This bead is the pile.

Measured 2026-08-06 on shady2k/feat-file-manager-2:
- `deadcode ./...` excluding node_modules: 86 unreachable funcs. It was 66 on
  2026-07-26 (recorded in nocx-ckoy.1). Twenty were added in eleven days.
- knip@5 on frontend/, zero-config: 118 unused exports, 127 unused exported
  types, 35 unused files, 1 unused dependency, 2 unused devDependencies,
  3 unlisted dependencies. These numbers are NOT yet trustworthy — knip emits a
  configuration hint that it has not been told the entry points, and an export
  used only by a file it wrongly considers unused is itself counted unused. The
  first honest number requires knip.json, which nocx-ckoy.1 delivers.

DO THIS BEAD AFTER nocx-ckoy.1, not before: the baseline file it produces IS the
work list, already deduplicated and already agreed, and the knip config is what
makes the frontend half real rather than an estimate.

Every entry is one of three things, and each gets a different action — the whole
point of the exercise is that they are not the same:

1. A feature that was never wired. It is a bug and it gets a bead, not a
   deletion: the vault (nocx-25k9.1) and history (nocx-rtg0) were both this, and
   both were found by exactly this kind of sweep. Deleting them would have been
   deleting the evidence.
2. A second implementation of something that already exists elsewhere. Known
   example already recorded in nocx-ckoy.1: internal/profile has BuildGroupTree
   and ResolveGroupPath while frontend/src/profiles.ts has live buildGroupTree()
   and resolveGroupPath() — the grouping logic exists twice and the Go copy is
   the dead one. Delete the dead copy, and say in the commit which one survived.
3. Genuinely dead. Delete it.

A batch commit that deletes N symbols without classifying them is the failure
mode here: it makes the number go to zero and loses the two beads that were
hiding in it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The baseline files committed by nocx-ckoy.1 are empty, OR every remaining entry
  carries an inline reason and a bead id.
- Each deletion commit names which of the three categories its entries were, and
  for category 2 names the surviving implementation.
- Every category-1 entry became a bead before its line was touched.
- The gate stays green throughout: this is a sequence of small commits, not one.
acceptance_criteria: The dead-code baselines are empty or every remaining entry carries a reason and a bead id; each deletion commit classifies its entries; every unwired-feature entry became a bead before deletion.

title: restoreDescriptor has four writers and no reader — and no gate asks that question
description:
Found while designing the file manager (nocx-gglz), by reading the code rather
than by any gate.

restoreDescriptor is written in four places — tabs.ts:456, tabs.ts:504,
main.tsx:226, state/tab-model.ts:255 — declared `readonly restoreDescriptor:
unknown` at tab-content.ts:143 and state/tab-model.ts:58, and READ NOWHERE.
Nothing serialises the tab list; nothing reconstructs a tab from a descriptor.
architecture.md:196 describes tab-restore ownership as though the mechanism
exists.

WHY NO LINTER SEES IT, precisely:

- tsc --strict checks that every ContentDescriptor SUPPLIES the field, because
  it is required. Nothing in a type system asks whether anybody consumes a
  value; that is whole-program dataflow, not typing.
- @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars scopes to bindings within a file. A
  property of an exported interface is out of scope by construction.
- noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters are not enabled in frontend/tsconfig.json,
  and would not have caught this if they were — same reason.
- `unused` in .golangci.yml and `deadcode` answer different questions ("is this
  symbol referenced?", "is it reachable from main?") and neither runs on TS.
- The declared type is `unknown`, so even a structural tool has nothing to trace.

THE SHAPE IS THE POINT. nocx-ckoy.1 is the sibling question on the Go side:
`unused` is silent because a symbol IS referenced, and reachability was the
missing question. nocx-rtg0 is the mirror image of this one: a reachable READ
path (Query) hid an unreachable WRITE path (ContentDB.Add) in the same package,
and `deadcode` was empty. Here it is a reachable WRITE path with no read path.
All three are "half a pipe", and no gate we run asks whether a pipe has two ends.

WHAT ACTUALLY FINDS IT is the rule AGENTS.md already states and this repo has
paid for twice: every epic that is not a chore proves its happy path end to end.
One automated check that restarts the app and asserts a tab comes back would
have reported the absence on day one. A tool is worth adding (knip finds unused
exports and files, and is cheap) but it is a floor, not the criterion — knip
would not have flagged a required interface field either.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. grep -rn "restoreDescriptor" frontend/src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx
2. Observe four writers, two declarations, zero readers.
3. Run the full gate: gofumpt, golangci-lint, go test -race, prettier, eslint,
   npm run typecheck, npm test. All green.
4. Run `deadcode ./...` — it says nothing, because it does not analyse
   TypeScript and because every writer is reachable from main.

## Acceptance Criteria

Exactly one of these is true, and the other is not:

- restoreDescriptor has a production reader that reconstructs tabs, proved by an
  automated check that restarts the app and asserts a tab comes back with its
  identity; or
- restoreDescriptor, its four writers and its two declarations are deleted, and
  the tab-restore-ownership paragraph at architecture.md:196 is removed or
  marked as deferred.

Leaving it as-is is not an available outcome: it is a documented capability that
does not exist, which is how the vault shipped unwired.

Separately: a decision is recorded, in the bead, on whether a frontend
dead-export gate (knip) joins the pre-commit gate — with the measured count of
what it finds today, so the decision is made against a number.
close_reason: Resolved by decision rather than by implementation, and the decision is recorded in the code. The file viewer that would have been the fifth writer passes restoreDescriptor: null instead, as main.tsx:226 already did — adding a writer while building on the finding would have been the same defect. The shape a restore reader should adopt is in a comment at the viewer. The underlying question 'should tab restore exist' is not this bead's and was never in scope for nocx-708q; the design's §5.6 lifecycle table has no app-restart row for exactly this reason, and D13 says only what is enforceable today: if and when restore lands, identity persists and bytes never do.

title: Host key check does not distinguish direct vs jump route to the same hostname
description:
When connecting to the same hostname directly and through a jump host, the host key is checked against the same known_hosts entry. If the server behind the jump is a different machine (different IP, different key) than the direct route, nocx reports host-key-changed even though both are correct for their respective paths.

The probe (connections.test) connects directly via dialDirect, so it sees the direct-route key. The open path connects through the jump host, which may resolve the hostname to a different server. The known_hosts entry written by the direct probe does not match the jump-route server.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Connect directly to a host (key accepted, written to known_hosts).
2. Connect to the same hostname through a jump host that resolves it to a different server.
3. Host key mismatch is reported.

Expected: the jump route's host key is verified independently (the known_hosts entry should distinguish routes, or the jump-route key should be accepted separately).
acceptance_criteria: A connection through a jump host to a hostname that has a different key than the direct route can be accepted and does not conflict with the direct-route known_hosts entry. The probe (connections.test) for a profile with a jump host connects through the jump to verify the key the open path will see.
notes:
Reopened after PR #63 review on 2026-08-06. Probe now follows the jump route, but the acceptance criterion that direct-route and jump-route keys coexist independently is still unmet: both routes still address the same known_hosts host entry. The frontend open-error handling also needs the existing explicit TOFU/changed-key dialog rather than automatic trust.
Reopened 2026-08-06: closed while the work was still only on PR #64, which is not merged. #64 was split into per-concern branches; this bead's work lives on one of them and is not on main yet.
close_reason: Merged to main while splitting PR #64 into per-concern branches.

title: Connections search filter appears not to work
description:
The user reports the 'Filter connections' input does not filter the list. Investigation found the wiring is correct: searchQuery signal (connections.tsx:364) feeds filteredProfiles memo (1763-1773) which filters by name/host/user substring. The filter tests (connections.behavior.test.tsx:206-266) pass. The likely cause is that the list cannot scroll (nocx-dzi1), so filtered results below the fold are invisible and the filter appears broken. If the scroll fix does not resolve it, reproduce in the real app and investigate further.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Settings > Connections with several entries.
2. Type a search query in the 'Filter connections' input.

Observed: the list does not appear to change. Expected: only matching connections are shown.
acceptance_criteria: Typing in the filter input narrows the list to matching connections. If the root cause is the scroll bug, this closes with nocx-dzi1.
close_reason: Merged to main while splitting PR #64 into per-concern branches.

title: SSH jump-host connection fails with attempted methods [none]
description:
When connecting through a jump host, the SSH handshake fails with 'attempted methods [none], no supported methods remain'. The jump host's ConnectConfig is dropped at the session→ssh seam: sshOptionsFromConfig (session.go:312-380) forwards only WithJumpHost(host,port,user,authMode), WithJumpCredentials and WithJumpPassphraseSecretID, but NEVER forwards cfg.JumpConfig, cfg.JumpKeyFile, or the jump hop's KeySecretID/PasswordRequester/UnlockRequester. acquirePooled rebuilds ConnectConfig from options, so JumpConfig==nil and JumpKeyFile=='' in production; acquireJumpHost's flat fallback then builds a jump config missing key file, vault key and both requesters; buildAuthChain yields zero real methods and dialJumpForConnect has no empty-auth guard.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a connection with a jump host (profile with JumpHost set).
2. Set the jump host's auth to publicKey (or inherit it from group defaults).
3. Connect.

Observed: 'ssh authentication failed ... attempted methods [none], no supported methods remain'. Expected: the jump host authenticates with the same methods as a direct connection.
acceptance_criteria: A jump host connection authenticates using the jump profile's resolved auth methods (key, password, agent). The jump hop's KeySecretID, PasswordRequester and UnlockRequester are forwarded through the session→ssh seam. An empty auth chain on a jump dial fails with ErrNoAuthMethod, not the raw handshake error.
close_reason: Merged to main while splitting PR #64 into per-concern branches.

title: Group members cannot be collapsed in the connections list
description:
The collapse feature does not exist. renderGroupSection (connections.tsx:1871-1905) renders group members unconditionally — there is no expanded/collapsed signal, no chevron toggle, no click handler on the group header. ProfileGroup has no persisted collapse state. The kit ships ChevronDownIcon for the toggle.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Settings > Connections with at least one group containing members.
2. Click the group header.

Observed: nothing happens — members are always visible. Expected: clicking the group header toggles member visibility, with a chevron indicating state.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a group header toggles its members' visibility. A chevron icon indicates expanded/collapsed state. The group header and its actions remain visible when collapsed.
close_reason: Merged to main while splitting PR #64 into per-concern branches.

title: Connections list does not scroll when there are many entries
description:
The height chain breaks at .cm-root (styles/surfaces/connections.css:6-9) which has no flex/min-height, and .ui-collection-view (styles/components/collection-view.css:1-5) which has min-height:0 but no flex:1 1 auto. The scroll owner .ui-collection-view__body (overflow-y:auto) never gets a bounded height, so the list grows to content and is clipped by .ui-page__contained's overflow:hidden. The wave-6 migration to CollectionView dropped the height propagation from the old .cm-body scroll owner.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Settings > Connections.
2. Import or create enough connections that the list exceeds the pane height.
3. Try to scroll the list.

Observed: the list is clipped, no scroll. Expected: the list scrolls within the pane.
acceptance_criteria: The connections list scrolls when there are more entries than fit in the pane. The Secrets page, which uses the same CollectionView, also scrolls.
close_reason: Merged to main while splitting PR #64 into per-concern branches.

title: e2e/history-persistence.spec.ts passes an obsolete XDG trio to VaultBackend and would crash at runtime
description:
Reported by the nocx-v64o worker while writing its own e2e: the spec constructs VaultBackend with the old three-argument XDG shape, which no longer exists. It is not exercised by the suites that run today, so nothing caught it.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run e2e/history-persistence.spec.ts.

## Acceptance Criteria
The spec constructs VaultBackend the way the product does now, and it runs in whatever job covers e2e — a spec nobody runs is not a test.

title: TestTunnelConn_DialAfterCloseFails flakes in the container on a 5s wall-clock wait
description:
The container gate failed once on 'Done did not close' after killConns; the same test passes locally with -count=6 both with and without the change under review, so the difference is the loaded container against a 5-second wall-clock deadline. A timing-sensitive assertion that only fails in company is the shape that erodes trust in the gate.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run the pre-commit container gate under load; occasionally internal/ssh fails at ssh_tunnel_test.go:316.

## Acceptance Criteria
The test waits on the event it means (the lease observing the loss) rather than on a fixed 5 seconds, or the deadline is derived from a stated budget with the reason written down. It passes under -count=20 with the CPU busy.
close_reason: Fix is on main and the gate that would catch a regression is green on ec3e2a7 (run 31246707047: backend, backend-linux x2, frontend, e2e all pass). Fixed by ded79bf — a kill that closes nothing is a test that waits for nothing.

title: The bootstrap passport names generation '-' when it skips an already-current publish
description:
launcher_publish.go exports NOCX_GENERATION only from a publish that actually happened, so the argv launcher's skip path (host already at this version) emits a passport whose generation field is '-'. The launch carrier always names the committed generation, so a steady-state installed host reports correctly, but a bootstrap onto an already-installed host records an observation with no generation.

## Steps to Reproduce
Publish a bundle on a host, drop the local installed fact (so the planner chooses bootstrap), connect again: the publish short-circuits as already-installed and the passport carries generation '-'.

## Acceptance Criteria
The passport names the generation that is ACTIVE on the host, whether or not this run published it — read from the verified manifest on the skip path — and a test asserts the skip path's passport bytes name it. Found by the P11 journey (nocx-q3y9).

title: Decide whether to hide the bootstrap echo at render, once the path is proven end to end
description: The owner deferred this on 2026-08-05: 'прятать строку при рендере можно, но сейчас мы этого делать не будем, вначале нужно протестировать'. The rewritten ssh line is ~190 bytes and visible by decision (ADR-0022 N2); no delivery mechanism shortens it meaningfully (207 -> 158 -> 130 bytes), so hiding at render is the only remaining way to remove it from the screen.
acceptance_criteria: Either the region between the B and C markers of a running block is not rendered — with a test proving async output landing in that window is not lost — or this bead is closed with the reason it stays visible. ADR-0004's rejection of renderer-side echo suppression is revisited explicitly, not silently.

title: P10 The footprint is visible and removable, even though it was never asked about
description: Package P10 of .internal/specs/2026-08-05-nocxify-delivery-modes-design.md (section 10). Read that spec first — it is committed on this branch.
acceptance_criteria: For a host with a committed bundle the product shows destination, generation and path, and offers an uninstall that removes only manifest-owned unmodified files and reports a conflict otherwise; new result schemas in contracts/ with generated TS and both conformance tests.
close_reason: Landed as 0a10bc1: fact-backed footprint status (no connect), profile-scoped uninstall through Publisher.Uninstall with the raw client kept inside internal/ssh, Settings>Connections>Remote footprint; review fixed a Solid early-return and a timing-dependent sh-publish assertion

title: A staged launcher outlives its command, so a history rerun re-triggers the bootstrap
description:
internal/shellintegration/stage.go removes stale staged launchers only on the next Stage call, never on a timer.

## Steps to Reproduce
Submit a hand-typed ssh, exit, then recall the rewritten line from the local shell history with Ctrl-R and run it. The bootstrap runs again because the staged file still exists.

## Acceptance Criteria
The wrapper consumes the staged payload exactly once; a later rerun of the same line takes the else branch. stage.go remains a safety net for abandoned files. Fixed in P4.
close_reason: Landed as 655d1c0: the staged payload is removed inside the command substitution, so a history rerun takes the else branch and the branch keeps ssh's status

title: Wire SSH completion adapter at composition root
description: Follow-up to nocx-w7h.15: wire the SSH completer at the composition root. Inject the SSH client as a DiscoveryConn provider so shell.complete on remote sessions creates per-request discovery leases. The local completer is already wired.
acceptance_criteria: On an SSH session to a bash host, typing 'ls /et' + Tab lists /etc/ from the remote host via the DiscoveryConn lane.
close_reason: Merged into nocx-w7h.15 — the SSH completer is wired at the composition root.

title: ports.pause has no caller now that the header action is Refresh
description:
`nocx-wzc4.11` replaced the Pause header action with Refresh, on the owner's
call and on the measurement: one sample is ~12 ms, so there was nothing to
protect a host from. The frontend pause control now only *reflects* a pause the
backend reports, and `ports.pause` has no caller in the renderer.

The capability itself is not obviously wrong — "do not poll this production
host" is a real wish — but it now lives nowhere a user can reach, which is the
shape `AGENTS.md` rule 2 names.

Decide deliberately: give it a home (a per-connection setting beside
`portDiscovery`, which is where a standing preference belongs, rather than a
button), or remove the RPC, its schema and the scheduler's pause path together.

## Steps to Reproduce

`grep -rn "services.pause\|ports.pause" frontend/src` finds the client method
and no caller.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Either a user can reach it, or it is gone from the transport, the contract and
  the scheduler in one commit.

title: The activity bar is one real view and a gear, which reads as an IDE waiting to be filled
description:
Review, 2026-08-04. The side panel is right — ports must coexist with the
terminal, so a tab would be wrong. The permanent VS Code activity bar around it
is the premature part: with one real view and a Settings gear it spends
horizontal space and visual identity on features that do not exist yet.

Ports is also not a workspace navigator like Explorer or Git. It is a
contextual instrument for the session in front of you, and it has nothing to
say on a local session with no listeners.

Options, in the reviewer's order of preference: a contextual companion dock
opened from a small services indicator near the context rail or tab strip, with
a count only when meaningful (`2 services`, `1 forwarded`, a warning); or, if
the rail is strategically committed, at least make the Ports icon contextual —
quiet or hidden where it has nothing to show, rather than a permanent dead
destination.

Do not lose: the keyboard reveal, the collapse-counts-as-hidden pause, or the
panel-beside-terminal placement.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open nocx with a local tab.
2. The activity bar shows one view icon and a gear; the view has nothing to say.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The panel is reachable without a permanent rail carrying a single
  destination, or the rail earns its space.
- Where there is nothing to show, the entry point is quiet rather than dead.

title: ssh completion only knows configured hosts, so a host you actually used is not offered
description:
Owner, 2026-08-04: "Где подсказки по ssh? Мы же вроде планировали это."

They are built and wired: `hostProvider` is registered in
`frontend/src/suggest/providers.ts:394` whenever a `ProfileClient` is present,
scoped to `ssh`'s argument position, ranked above history. What it can offer is
the union of saved profiles and `~/.ssh/config` aliases — and nothing else.

So `ssh pi@192.168.0.93`, typed at a Raspberry Pi that is neither a saved
profile nor an alias, has nothing to complete against. Worse in a dev build:
the dev profile directory is separate by design (`internal/storage/appdir.go`),
so a developer's real saved profiles are not there at all and only aliases
remain.

The host you actually connected to yesterday is the one you are most likely to
want, and we already record commands. A history-derived host source would have
offered it the second time.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `ssh pi@192.168.0.93` in a tab, successfully.
2. Later, type `ssh ` and ask for completion. The host is not offered.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A host reached by a hand-typed `ssh` is offered afterwards, ranked below
