acceptance_criteria: A tracked file modified since HEAD shows a marker; an ignored entry is dimmed; markers are read-only and never block the tree from rendering when git is absent or the directory is not a repo.

title: File viewer: syntax highlighting
description:
The viewer ships as plain monospaced text because CodeMirror is not in the project. It arrives with nocx-2gf.
Deferred out of nocx-708q by the design in .internal/specs/2026-08-01-file-manager-design.md (nocx-gglz). Depends on the file manager existing.
acceptance_criteria: An opened source file is highlighted by language, read-only, in both local and remote viewers; an unknown extension falls back to plain monospace without error.

title: Files panel: recursive name search, not a filter over loaded nodes
description:
nocx-708q deliberately shipped no filter rather than a half one: a filter over lazily-loaded nodes silently fails to find files that exist, which is worse than no control at all. A recursive walk is real work and on SFTP it is a chain of round-trips, so it is its own bead.
Deferred out of nocx-708q by the design in .internal/specs/2026-08-01-file-manager-design.md (nocx-gglz). Depends on the file manager existing.
acceptance_criteria: Typing in the search box finds files anywhere under the root, including in directories never expanded, on BOTH providers; the remote implementation bounds its walk and reports when it stopped early. Tested with a match that exists only in an unexpanded directory — the case a filter over loaded nodes cannot pass.

title: editor.ts and style.css cite nocx-6w4z for a change that bead is not about
description: Found while answering a W1 worker question on 2026-08-01. The hide()/reservation removal in frontend/src/editor.ts (the comment block ending 'the jump comes back and is the smaller of the two problems') and the matching note in frontend/src/style.css both cite (nocx-6w4z). That bead is titled 'Switching strip orientation marks every inactive tab as having activity', which is a different defect. Either the comments cite the wrong id or the work landed under a bead that does not describe it. Low value on its own; it costs real time when someone traces a deliberate decision back to its reasoning and lands on an unrelated bug — which is exactly what happened here. Find the right id or file one retroactively and correct both comments.
acceptance_criteria: Both comments cite a bead whose title describes the reservation removal.

title: Per-entry streaming notifications on the control plane
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-31-command-blocks-history-syntax-design.md §6.5. Server-to-client notifications exist (exit, settings.changed, vault.changed) but are BROADCASTS. An agent turn needs per-entry streamed chunks — ledger.chunk {entryId, seq, data} — with ordering and backpressure of its own.

Filed now, ahead of agent mode, so that epic does not discover a missing transport capability mid-flight. The binary data plane stays PTY-only: wrapping model tokens in binary frames would put a second protocol on a plane whose entire contract is 'these bytes go to a terminal'.
acceptance_criteria: Chunks for two concurrent entries interleave on the wire without corrupting either. A slow consumer applies backpressure rather than growing an unbounded buffer. The data plane carries no non-PTY payload.

title: Output is data: lenses, diffs, and reports
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-07-31-command-blocks-history-syntax-design.md §10.11, §10.12. Deferred — the seams (derived text, derivedFrom, cites edges) are built by earlier epics; this epic spends them.

Lenses: registered transformers deriving views over derived text — JSON tree, failing tests, compiler diagnostics, changed files, URLs — including as a per-block inspector panel rather than a separate surface (a separate surface would be a second vocabulary for one concept, which is the defect two kit epics were spent unwinding).

Diff of two runs: 'what changed between the run that worked and the one that did not'. Diffing raw VT is meaningless — cursor moves and colour resets swamp the signal — so this is a capability derived text creates rather than exposes.

Export as markdown: the local-first answer to a cloud share link, honouring sensitivity.

Paste provenance: the cites edge only. NOT a clipboard history surface — see §14.
acceptance_criteria: A JSON payload in output can be browsed as a tree without leaving the terminal. Two runs of the same command can be diffed on their derived text. An entry exports as markdown with its environment, status and duration, and a sensitive entry refuses without an explicit override.

title: Settings and key-material secrets now appear in the Secrets list
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Store private key material on a connection.
2. Open Settings → Secrets.

## Expected
The list shows what the surface says it shows — passwords and key passphrases.

## Actual
Key-material and settings-owned secrets surface too, because the inventory is now built from the vault's own records rather than from credential password/passphrase references. Reported by the worker implementing ADR-0016; a consequence of the change, not a defect in it.
acceptance_criteria: Decide what Secrets lists now that the vault knows everything it holds, and make the page's description match.

title: A secret's derived label is empty when the credential has no username
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a credential with a name but no username, save a password on it.
2. Settings -> Secrets.
3. The row reads "SSH password for" — nothing after "for" — then "1 connection".

## Why

The label rule in internal/vault/inventory.go composes "SSH password for <user>@<host>:<port>"
for a single-use secret and "SSH password for <user>" for a shared one. With no username both
collapse to a dangling preposition.

Minor: the row is still identifiable by its usage count and its store. But the point of a
derived label is that the user never has to invent one, and an empty one makes them guess
anyway.
acceptance_criteria: A password on a credential with no username produces a label a human can act on — naming the connection or the host rather than trailing off. A test covers the no-username case, which is the one the current rule does not.

title: Import a key from a host you are already connected to
description:
Asked during the Secrets/Vault design review and deferred there deliberately.

Two readings, and only one is coherent. Recording a PATH on a remote host is meaningless: our SSH client runs locally, so a path on the far side is not something it can open — that only makes sense for jump-host semantics, which is a different feature (nocx-wzc4 territory). READING the key off the host into our vault is coherent and technically possible, since we already hold a session.

Deferred because the cost is out of proportion to the gap it closes:

- It needs a dedicated non-interactive exec channel. Reading key material out of the user's interactive PTY is forbidden by AD-6 (the backend never sniffs the byte stream) and would also leave the private key in the scrollback.
- A remote file browser (SFTP, or exec plus ls, with permissions, symlinks and error states) exists nowhere in the product today.
- nocx-25k9.16's paste path already covers the case at the cost of one extra step: cat the key on the host, paste it here.

Worth checking before this is ever built: whether the real need behind it is agent forwarding rather than moving key material at all. That is a different and cheaper feature.
acceptance_criteria: From the key input, an option reads a private key off a host the user already has a session with and stores it in the vault. The bytes travel a dedicated non-interactive exec channel, never the interactive PTY, and never reach the renderer or the scrollback. The user is shown what will be read and from where before it happens.

title: Auto-seal goroutine has no exit path
description:
The auto-seal goroutine started in vault.New (internal/vault/vault.go:109) has no exit path: its for/select loop has no quit case and Vault has no Close. In production that is one goroutine for the process lifetime, which is harmless. In tests every testVault() creates one, so the vault suite leaves dozens blocked on channels, each holding its Vault alive.

Not urgent and not user-visible. It becomes visible the day someone adds a goleak check, or if the app ever constructs more than one Vault.

## Steps to Reproduce

    grep -n 'go v.autoSealLoop' internal/vault/vault.go
    grep -n 'func (v \*Vault) autoSealLoop' -A 40 internal/vault/vault.go   # no quit case

## Acceptance Criteria

Vault owns the goroutine's lifetime: a Close (or a context passed to New) stops the loop, tests call it, and a goleak assertion in the vault package proves nothing outlives a test. If the decision is instead that a process-lifetime goroutine is correct here, say so in a comment at the loop and close this as wontfix — but decide it rather than leaving it implicit.
close_reason: Fixed in cdc21e7: Vault.Close stops the auto-seal goroutine and seals, is idempotent, and the App holds it as interface{ Close() } and calls it after the transport stops. The test measures a goroutine delta across a batch of twenty and was verified to fail without the fix (22 outlive Close). testVault now registers t.Cleanup(v.Close) so the suite stops leaking.

title: Step 2: offer visual companion just-in-time if a visual question arises
close_reason: Visual companion not offered: no mockup/layout question arose — all forks were conceptual (platform availability, key hierarchy, seal scope). V2 (Vault page) will revisit if a layout question comes up.

title: Evaluate Stryker for TypeScript mutation testing
description:
## Why

Sibling of nocx-u4b, which chose gremlins for Go. The frontend has 990 tests and no measure of
whether they assert on behaviour or merely execute it.

## Candidate

StrykerJS. There is no serious competitor for TypeScript — the alternatives are unmaintained.
It matters that it ships @stryker-mutator/vitest-runner, because this repo runs Vitest, and
that it has an incremental mode, because the cost is otherwise prohibitive.

## Constraint, same as nocx-u4b

Mutation testing reruns the suite once per mutant. The frontend suite is ~12s for 990 tests,
and a file the size of connections.tsx generates hundreds of mutants. This CANNOT go in the
pre-commit hook — that hook was deliberately brought from 67s to 3-29s (nocx-ro3h) and putting
this in it would undo that and more. A separate make target, run on demand, scoped.

## Where to point it first

Pure functions with real branching, where a surviving mutant means something specific:

- `frontend/src/profiles.ts` — parseQuickConnect and decideSaveRoute. decideSaveRoute has 8
  tests for a pure router; whether they pin the routing or just execute it is exactly the
  question this tool answers.
- `frontend/src/connections.tsx` — the largest surface, and the one where a silently wrong
  branch costs the most.

## What it will and will not buy — record this honestly

It measures the quality of tests that EXIST. Most defects found while reviewing worker output
in the 2026-07-29 session were tests that were ABSENT, and for those the mutation score is
uninformative — you do not need mutation testing to notice zero tests, you need to read the
diff.

The one case it would have caught: `ComputeCredentialUsage` returned a nil slice where the
wire contract required an empty array. The Go test asserted `len(refs) == 0`, which passes for
both, so `[]ProfileRef{} -> nil` is a mutant that would have survived and pointed straight at
it. That class — an assertion too weak to distinguish two states the wire distinguishes — is
what this is for.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A make target runs Stryker over a named scope, not the whole frontend.
- Surviving mutants are triaged into beads or dismissed with a stated reason.
- The score is used as a finder, not a gate. A number in CI becomes a target, and the cheapest
  way to raise it is assertion-free tests that kill mutants incidentally — which is worse than
  no measure at all.

title: A one-off ssh_config importer, labelled as producing a detached copy
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

Spec section 4.

- An importer sits alongside the Tabby one in Export / Backup / Import.
- It is labelled honestly: it produces a DETACHED COPY, not a synchronised view. An imported
  record freezes one evaluation of a positional config, and later edits to an earlier wildcard
  block, an Include, a Match condition or alias ordering silently do not reach it.
- The live source remains the default path. This exists for people who want to take ownership
  of a host, not as the way aliases normally appear.
close_reason: A one-off importer sits beside the Tabby one under Export / Backup / Import, labelled as producing a detached copy. It stores the RESOLVED hostname, deliberately unlike adoption which stores the alias: a detached copy is meant to freeze one evaluation of a positional config, which is exactly what the label warns about. Collision policy is skip-by-name-or-host, stated and tested. Coordinator removed a second renderer-side id minting here too. Noted and left: the collision check string-matches the backend error text, which is the fragility the typed-error work (nocx-3isn) exists to remove.

title: light.css: semantic colours fall below any usable contrast floor
description:
Measured while adding the theme catalogue (nocx-7o42): light.css puts
--color-success at 2.69:1 on --color-canvas, and .nocx-chip-ok paints chip TEXT
with it. --color-accent is 4.22:1, below AA for text.

The theme-catalogue contrast gate deliberately excludes the semantic tokens for
this reason — fixing them means redesigning light.css, which did not belong in a
commit that adds themes.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Switch the theme to Light in Settings → Interface.
2. Run a command that exits 0 and look at the green exit chip (.nocx-chip-ok),
   which paints its text with --color-success (#16a34a) on --color-canvas
   (#e6e8ed) — 2.69:1, against a 4.5:1 requirement for text.

## Acceptance Criteria

- light.css --color-success, --color-warning and --color-danger each reach 4.5:1
  on --color-canvas and --color-surface.
- TEXT_TOKENS in frontend/src/theme-catalogue.test.ts is widened to cover the
  three semantic tokens, and the whole catalogue passes.

title: The connection list is a type register smaller than the navigation beside it
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Settings -> Connections.
2. Compare the settings rail on the left with the connection list next to it.

Expected: two columns of navigable rows read as the same kind of thing.
Actual: at base 14px the rail is `--font-size-md` (14px) and the connection row
name was `--font-size-sm` (12.25px), with its second line at `--font-size-2xs`
(10.5px). The right-hand list read as a footnote to the left-hand one.

## What made it a defect rather than a choice

`.ui-settings-rail` sets its size and says why: "this surface primary navigation
rather than fine print". The connection list is the same job on the same screen
and made the opposite choice with no reason recorded — so nothing said which of
the two was right, and both looked deliberate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The connection row name matches the settings rail: body size.
- The second line is one step down, not two.
- The group caption is not smaller than the rows it heads; it separates itself
  with weight and colour.
- Nothing in the list sits below `--font-size-sm`.
close_reason: The connection list is body-sized like the settings rail beside it, its second line one step down, and nothing in it below sm. The rail's own rule already said why — primary navigation rather than fine print — and the list had made the opposite choice with no reason recorded.

title: The vertical strip's width is draggable and remembered
description:
The strip is a fixed 240px (`tab-strip.css`). Two lines of text per row make that a real constraint: a deep cwd or a long `user@host` ellipses at a width the user cannot change, and a narrow window has no way to reclaim the space.

The width is a preference, so it belongs with the others: a setting the strip reads, not a number in a stylesheet. The mechanism already exists — settings are declared in `internal/settings/settings.go`, delivered through the snapshot, and applied live by `SettingsObserver`; `tab.placement` is the working example.

The drag itself is the part with edges: a splitter between the strip and the panes, a minimum below which rows stop being readable, and the terminal's resize — the panes must re-fit as the strip moves, which is the same viewport path a window resize takes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Dragging the strip's inner edge resizes it live, and the terminal grid re-fits as it moves rather than after it stops.
- The width persists across a restart, and is clamped to a documented minimum and maximum.
- The setting reaches the strip through the settings snapshot, not through a second storage path.
- Nothing about the horizontal strip changes.

title: Each tab row carries a glyph for the kind of session it is
description:
Warp puts a round icon at the head of every row — a shell prompt for a terminal, an avatar for an agent session. It reads faster than the title, because the kind of a session is what you scan for first.

We have the fact already (`descriptor.surfaceType`) and the icon vocabulary is thin: `src/ui/icons/` holds three glyphs today. This is mostly deciding the set — local shell, SSH, service surface (Settings) — and drawing them in the same Lucide-derived style the existing icons use, at a size that comes from the type scale rather than a number.

Not the avatar: an agent session's picture is a network resource and a whole different question.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every row in the vertical strip shows a glyph naming its kind, and the glyph differs between a local terminal, an SSH session and Settings.
- The glyphs live in `src/ui/icons/` and are exported from its barrel, like every other icon.
- The row's layout does not shift when a glyph is absent or slow — the slot is reserved.
- No raw `px` font-size or hard-coded colour is introduced (the CSS gates stay at zero).

title: Quick-connect selected row may not show its accent fill — re-check on a fresh load
description:
Reported on 2026-07-27 from a screenshot. The rule is present in the stylesheet (accent fill, canvas text) and the screenshot may predate a reload, so this may be nothing.

Re-check on a running page before treating it as a defect. Filed rather than dropped because 'the rule is present' is exactly what was true of every defect in nocx-u7wq, all of which were valid CSS that did not apply.

title: Form row spacing in the connections form — gap may not be reaching the fields
description:
Reported on 2026-07-27 and NOT measured. The suspicion is that `gap` on `.cm-form-section` does not reach the fields because of an intervening wrapper, but nothing was verified — treat the cause as unknown.

Measure before fixing. This surface is being rewritten by the kit migration (nocx-pp3y), so check whether the symptom still exists before spending time on it.

title: Focus survival after a tab reorder is unverified
description:
Reported honestly by the nocx-82l9.5 worker rather than left silent: node identity across reorder is asserted with isSameNode and passes, but focus is not. jsdom shows focus loss that may be an artefact of its incomplete focus model, and no e2e spec covers focus after reorder, so neither result is evidence.

Low priority because reorder is a deliberate drag gesture and the tab is clicked to begin with — but it is exactly the kind of regression a keyboard user would hit and nobody would report.
acceptance_criteria: An e2e spec in both engines focuses a tab button, reorders the strip by drag, and asserts document.activeElement is still that button. The jsdom unit test is not sufficient — its focus model is incomplete, which is why this gap exists.
close_reason: Focus did NOT survive a drag reorder in either orientation on either engine: Solid's <For> clears focused state when reconciliation moves a node via insertBefore, even keyed by id — node identity surviving was necessary and not sufficient. Fixed by saving and restoring activeElement across reorder. Coordinator fixed two flakes in the new spec, both the same cause: fixed timeouts instead of polling the observable outcome. Five consecutive clean runs, 4/4.

title: Probe bead for JSON shape
description:
probe

## Acceptance Criteria

probe
close_reason: probe bead, deleting

title: [epic] Transport runtime modes: dev-verbose, production-quiet
description:
Homeless child of nocx-k0xk given its own epic: nocx-772 is not a quality gate and not dev tooling, it is a feature of the transport.

Suggested by the owner while diagnosing origin/host rejections: show rejection detail only in dev and CI, and rate-limit rejections in production. The concept does not exist yet — the nearest thing is nocx-hl3's OriginPolicy, already injected per runtime mode (LoopbackOriginPolicy for development, PinnedOriginPolicy for production), so the distinction exists in one place and needs generalising rather than inventing.

DONE WHEN: the transport has an explicit runtime mode, verbose auth logging appears only in dev/CI, rejections are rate-limited in production, and the mode is set at the composition root rather than sniffed.
acceptance_criteria: the transport has an explicit runtime mode, verbose auth logging appears only in dev/CI, rejections are rate-limited in production, and the mode is set at the composition root rather than sniffed.

title: [epic] Secret lifecycle hygiene: orphan collection and redaction
description:
Carved out of nocx-6ek. Unclaimed, and needs design before implementation — recorded so it is visibly deferred rather than quietly forgotten.

- nocx-dm0: the credential delete cascade is best-effort by design (ADR-0011 section 4 prefers a brief unreachable orphan over metadata pointing at a missing secret), so orphans accumulate and nothing collects them. The janitor needs a design first: when it runs, what it may delete, and how it proves a secret is unreferenced.
- nocx-23v: mask known secrets in rendered scrollback, the command ledger and clipboard export. A large feature on its own — it beats Tabby (vault, no redaction) and Warp (redaction, no vault) by combining both.

DONE WHEN: orphaned secrets are collected by a mechanism whose safety argument is written down, and a secret injected from the vault never appears in scrollback, ledger or clipboard.
acceptance_criteria: orphaned secrets are collected by a mechanism whose safety argument is written down, and a secret injected from the vault never appears in scrollback, ledger or clipboard.

title: [epic] Windows and Linux support
description:
macOS is the first and only target today (docs/vision.md section 8), but ADR-0007 commits to cross-platform auto-update, so the other platforms are a stated direction rather than a maybe. This epic is where that direction accumulates instead of leaking into macOS-shaped epics as stray P3 children.

- nocx-6ek.1: storage.NewOSPaths returns 'unsupported platform' for any GOOS outside linux/darwin, so app.New() cannot start on Windows at all. ADR-0011 names only the XDG and Application Support layouts. Decide deliberately: add the %AppData%/%LocalAppData% layout, or state the refusal as intentional and record why.

DONE WHEN: the platform question is answered deliberately — either nocx starts and stores its data correctly on Windows and Linux, or the refusal is documented as a decision with its reasoning, and no epic elsewhere carries a stray cross-platform child.
acceptance_criteria: The platform question is answered deliberately — either nocx starts and stores its data correctly on Windows and Linux, or the refusal is documented as a decision with its reasoning, and no epic elsewhere carries a stray cross-platform child.
close_reason:
Closed on its own DONE WHEN, which reads: 'the platform question is answered deliberately — either nocx starts and stores its data correctly on Windows and Linux, or the refusal is documented as a decision with its reasoning, and no epic elsewhere carries a stray cross-platform child.'

The second branch is now taken. Owner decision, 2026-07-26: Windows is not planned. Recorded with its reasoning on the epic's only child, nocx-6ek.1, which is closed rather than dropped — the question was answered, not abandoned.

The Linux half needed nothing: it already works. platform_linux.go implements the updater's Platform seam, AppImage release builds ship in CI (nocx-mbu), and storage.NewOSPaths handles the XDG layout. The epic paired the two platforms because ADR-0007 committed to cross-platform auto-update, but only one of them was ever missing.

CARRY-FORWARD, and it is a real one: ADR-0007 still commits to cross-platform auto-update, which now overstates the intent. That decision record should get a superseding note rather than a quiet edit — the same standard applied to ADR-0001 when wterm was removed. Flagged to the owner; not done here, because amending a decision record is the owner's call.

title: storage.NewOSPaths refuses to run on Windows
description:
internal/storage/paths.go returns 'unsupported platform' for any GOOS outside linux/darwin, so app.New() cannot start on Windows at all. That is the honest behaviour for today (ADR-0011 names only the XDG and Application Support layouts, and macOS is the first target), but ADR-0007 commits to cross-platform auto-update, so Windows is a stated direction. Decide deliberately: either add the %AppData%/%LocalAppData% layout, or record in ADR-0011 that Windows is out of scope for persistence.

## Acceptance Criteria
Either Windows path roles resolve, or ADR-0011 states Windows is out of scope and the error message points at that decision.
close_reason:
Answered deliberately, which is what this bead asked for: Windows is NOT a supported platform, and the refusal in storage.NewOSPaths is intentional rather than an oversight.

Owner decision, 2026-07-26: Windows support is not planned. The bead offered two branches — add the %AppData%/%LocalAppData% layout, or state the refusal as intentional and record why — and this is the second.

Reasoning, so a future reader does not treat this as a gap to fill: nocx is macOS-first (docs/vision.md section 8) with Linux working today (platform_linux.go, AppImage release builds). Windows is a third path with its own storage layout, its own bundle-swap semantics for the updater, its own signing story and its own terminal/PTY behaviour — a cost nobody is currently buying. The code already refuses rather than half-working, which is the honest failure mode: app.New() cannot start on Windows at all, so there is no silent misbehaviour to discover later.

Not permanent, just not planned. Reversing it means adding a Platform implementation behind the existing seam (nocx-kv0) and a Windows branch in NewOSPaths — the seams are in place, so the decision is cheap to revisit if the answer changes.

title: Runtime modes for the transport: gate verbose auth logging and rate-limit rejections
description:
Suggested by the owner while diagnosing the origin/host rejections: show rejection details only in dev/CI.

The concept does not exist yet. The nearest thing is nocx-hl3's OriginPolicy, which is already injected 'per runtime mode' (LoopbackOriginPolicy for development, PinnedOriginPolicy for production) — so a mode distinction is implied but never named. Wiring log verbosity to the same switch would be coherent, and pinning the production Origin is the natural moment to introduce it.

Deliberately NOT done now, and the reasoning should survive:

Production is the one environment where the failure cannot be reproduced. In dev and CI a developer can attach a debugger, add output and re-run; on a user's machine the log is all there is. A rejected upgrade in production means either a bug or a real attack, and both need the Origin and Host that were rejected. Hiding them there removes the evidence exactly where it is irreplaceable. This is not hypothetical: the first version of that log omitted the values on 'attacker-controlled text' grounds, and 36 rejections per CI run were misread as suite flakiness for hours.

What IS worth building here:
- a named runtime mode (dev / CI / production) with the origin policy and log verbosity both keyed off it, rather than two independent switches;
- rate limiting on rejection logs. Log growth under a rejection flood is the real operational concern, and it is solved by capping frequency, not by discarding the fields that make a log useful.

If verbosity does get gated, keep Origin and Host in production and gate something else — the useful distinction is probably per-request detail versus an aggregate counter, not detail versus nothing.

title: STORE-7: export, import and backup as distinct modes
description:
ADR-0011 section 7. With a keychain in the middle there is no honest 'back up everything' unless the app reads secrets back out. So: configuration export (profiles, groups, credential metadata, settings; secret references present but unresolved); portable encrypted export (explicit, user-authenticated, encrypted under a new passphrase — not part of normal persistence); same-machine backup (documents + content.db, plus a plain statement that secrets stay in the OS keychain); import (metadata first, then the user maps existing credentials or supplies missing secrets).

Private content — conversations, command history — is never silently included in a portable export. It is frequently more sensitive than the host metadata beside it.
acceptance_criteria: Each mode exists separately and states what it does and does not carry. No mode silently exports private content or resolved secrets.
close_reason:
STORE-7 core landed: internal/export implements the four ADR-0011 §7 modes as distinct operations — configuration export (SecretID references present, material never), portable encrypted export (NaCl secretbox + Argon2id from x/crypto, no new go.mod dependency, private content only on explicit opt-in), same-machine backup (reports content.db absent rather than failing, since internal/content is still a stub), and import (metadata first, reports unresolved credentials, never invents or resolves a secret). Each mode states what it carries and what it omits as data the UI can display, not as a source comment. 18 tests.

The guarantee is structural: internal/export does not import credential.SecretStore at all — the only mention in the package is a doc comment — so no mode can resolve a secret even by mistake. Verified independently, along with go.mod/go.sum being unchanged.

Closing on the acceptance criteria as written, which are about the modes and their guarantees. The user-facing surface is NOT here: there are no export RPCs and no UI entry points yet. That is filed separately so it stays visible in bd ready.

title: Design: scrollback separator visibility when there are no frozen blocks
description:
Open question Q4 from spike/dom-scrollback/DESIGN-NOTES.md, left unresolved when nocx-4ff.18 closed.

The separator between the DOM block stack and the live xterm region is shown only when at least one frozen block exists, and hidden during alt-screen (frontend/src/scrollback/controller.ts:210). On a fresh session — and again after every clear — there are no blocks, so the live region touches the top of the scrollback area with no boundary. Whether that reads as clean or as disorienting is a taste call the owner has not made.

Options: keep the current conditional behaviour; always show the separator so the live region always has a lid; or show a lighter always-on rule that gains contrast once blocks exist.

Decide live in the browser dev loop against a real session, then record the choice here.
acceptance_criteria:
• The owner picks one of the three behaviours against a running session (fresh, after clear, with blocks, in and out of alt-screen).
• The chosen behaviour is implemented in _updateSeparator() and covered by the existing controller tests.
• DESIGN-NOTES.md Q4 is updated from open question to resolved.

title: SSH sessions miss COLORTERM=truecolor — TUIs fall back to 256 colors over SSH
description:
Surfaced by the alt-screen color investigation in the DOM-scrollback work (spike/dom-scrollback/DESIGN-NOTES.md, 'Alt-screen color fix P0-3').

Local PTY sessions export COLORTERM=truecolor (internal/pty/pty_local.go:121). The SSH path does not: internal/ssh/ssh_real.go:460 sends the pty-req with Term: 'xterm-256color' and no COLORTERM anywhere in the package. Modern TUIs (including claude) probe COLORTERM for truecolor capability, so the same program renders with a poorer palette over SSH than locally.

Note the constraint: env vars over SSH are subject to the remote sshd's AcceptEnv, so an env request may be silently refused. The reliable fallback is to export it from the shell-integration rc that nocx already installs remotely (see nocx-ccn).

## Acceptance Criteria

• A truecolor-probing program run over an nocx SSH session sees COLORTERM=truecolor.
• The mechanism degrades quietly when the remote sshd refuses the env request — no error surfaced to the user, no broken session.
• Covered by a test at whichever layer sets it (ssh_real_test.go for the request, or the shell-integration script tests).

title: devharness: pin WS port via env (NOCX_WS_PORT), drop the socat bridge
description: The VM->Mac browser dev loop (memory dev-loop-vm-mac-browser) currently needs a socat bridge because cmd/devharness listens on a random loopback port while the frontend fallback is fixed 9876. Let devharness honor NOCX_WS_PORT (default 0 = random as today) and restart becomes trivial; socat can be dropped. Dev-only seam: nocx-byc rejected this for the shipped app, devharness is untracked dev tooling.

title: SFTP file browser panel over active SSH session
description: Tabby-style SFTP panel: browse remote fs, upload/download, drag-and-drop. Builds on the 9le channel work; distinct from nocx-ccn (SFTP shell-integration install).
notes:
NARROWED 2026-08-01 (.internal/specs/2026-08-01-file-manager-design.md, nocx-gglz): this bead keeps upload, download and drag-drop transfer.

Read-only remote LISTING and READING move into nocx-708q, where they ship as the sftp implementation
of the shared filesystem Provider. Leaving listing here would have had two epics build it twice.

title: Secret redaction: mask known secrets in scrollback, ledger, clipboard
description: Secrets injected from the vault (Phase 2) are known to the app by construction, so mask them everywhere: rendered scrollback, command-ledger, clipboard export. Beats Tabby (vault, no redaction) and Warp (redaction, no vault) by combining both.

title: Workflows: saved parameterized commands with named args
description: Warp Drive parity minus cloud: save a command template with named arguments, fill via a small form, run from palette or editor. Local storage only.

title: Notification when a long command finishes (terminal unfocused)
description: Desktop notification when a command longer than N seconds exits while the window/tab is not focused. Duration comes from ledger C->D timestamps; click focuses the tab and scrolls to the block.

title: Block output: filter in place + download as file
description: Per-block output tools (Orca reference): filter output lines in place (substring first, regex later) and download the block output as a file.

title: Fail-closed enhanced: frontend still opens enhanced=true when backend denied marker-only
description:
Review follow-up (non-blocking, cosmetic, rare). When `newSessionID` fails (crypto/rand error), backend `ActivationEnv` fails closed and omits NOCX_PROMPT_MODE/NOCX_SESSION_ID — but the frontend already opened the session with `enhanced=true`, so the shell runs baseline (visible prompt + B markers) while the frontend still tries to own input → the DOM editor can appear over a VISIBLE prompt. User is not trapped (fail-open still holds); only cosmetic, and only on a rand failure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- On the fail-closed path the frontend does not present the editor over a visible prompt (e.g. backend signals that enhanced was denied for the session, or the frontend confirms marker-only actually engaged before owning input).

title: PTY-based regression test for OSC 133 C-marker latch
description: nocx-bvo (dup C markers) is fixed via a per-line latch but only verified by inspection — the DEBUG-trap path needs an interactive shell to exercise. Add a creack/pty-driven test that runs 'ls | grep x' in a real interactive bash and asserts exactly one 133;C per entered line. PR #1 / nocx-5mn.4.

title: [bash] array-form PROMPT_COMMAND (bash 5.1+) loses elements beyond [0]
description: nocx.bash captures __nocx_old_pc="$PROMPT_COMMAND" as a scalar; on bash>=5.1 where PROMPT_COMMAND can be an array, only element 0 is preserved and the user's other prompt commands are dropped. Handle the array form. Review finding #7, PR #1 / nocx-5mn.4.

title: Agent mode: AgentInputTarget on the same editor
description: Second InputTarget routing submit to the LLM controller on the SAME editor, with separate draft + history and an explicit mode indicator. Depends on the InputTarget abstraction and the editor surface.
acceptance_criteria: Switching to agent mode routes submit to the LLM path; drafts/histories are per-mode; editor layout/selection/completion UI are shared.
notes:
2026-07-25: RESOLVED — Pi does support driving the agent loop without its TUI. Verified against the locally installed build (pi 0.80.10, /nix/store/...-pi-coding-agent-0.80.10/bin/pi) plus pi.dev docs:
  --mode rpc    JSON protocol over stdin/stdout, documented as being FOR NON-NODE INTEGRATIONS — i.e. exactly a Go host
  --mode json   event stream for programmatic consumption
  --print / -p  non-interactive one-shot
  sessions      --session-id / --session / --fork / --resume, tree-structured storage
  --provider / --model / --api-key  bring-your-own model, incl. local
  SDK           Node embedding (not our path; we are Go)

CONSEQUENCE: agent mode is NOT agent-as-TUI. Driving pi --mode rpc as a child process keeps the session out of ALT_SCREEN, so the DOM editor retains input ownership and we render the dialog ourselves — which is the whole point of AgentInputTarget in ADR-0004 section 3.

SHAPE: a Go module behind an interface (AD-8) speaking JSON over stdio to the pi child. We already speak JSON-RPC 2.0 on the control plane (AD-1), so this is a familiar dialect, not a new one.
RENDERING: prompt -> response is structurally identical to command -> output, so agent turns become blocks in the DOM scrollback and reuse the ledger and block model rather than inventing a chat pane.
CONTEXT: 'context from current work' = the ledger (cwd, host, exit codes, durations) + block output, fed into pi's context; pi's --session-id gives a tab a durable conversation.
ALIGNMENT: bring-your-own-model matches vision.md:75 Phase 3 verbatim.

NEXT: read docs/rpc.md from the pi package for the actual wire shape before designing.
This bead is now much bigger than 'AgentInputTarget on the same editor' — likely wants promoting to its own epic.

title: Copy folder path action (from OSC 7 cwd)
description: Deferred out of nocx-5mn.2, whose bead mentioned it: the cwd is now tracked live via OSC 7, but there is no way to copy it. Needs its own UI wiring — clipboard API plus a keyboard shortcut and/or an entry in the context menu being designed in nocx-b05.
acceptance_criteria: The current folder path can be copied to the clipboard from the tab.

title: [bug] Text squeezes for a frame when a window resize starts
description: Reported by the owner while verifying nocx-q18: dragging the window edge briefly squashes the already-rendered text before it settles. Distinct from the glyph corruption that was just fixed — nothing is mangled, the frame is simply wrong. Likely mechanism: the WebGL canvas is stretched to the new window size immediately, while the grid is only recomputed after the ResizeObserver debounce (RESIZE_MIN_INTERVAL = 32ms) plus a rAF in frontend/src/renderers/xterm.ts, so at least one frame shows the old glyphs scaled to the new box. Worth checking how Tabby/VS Code avoid it — options include not scaling the canvas until the fit lands, or repainting synchronously on the first resize event rather than after the debounce.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging a window edge never shows a squashed or stretched frame of the previous content.
close_reason:
Landed at f2e235a. The bug still reproduced, but NOT for the reason it was filed — the worker established that, which is what I asked for.

The mechanism the bead described (32ms debounce plus an XtermRenderer ResizeObserver) was already gone, removed by the geometry rewrite. The remaining one-frame glitch was introduced BY that rewrite, and by MY brief: I asked for 'raw observer callbacks coalesced per animation frame', which produced a requestAnimationFrame wrapper around viewport delivery. That wrapper coalesced nothing — ResizeObserver already fires once per frame, after layout and before paint, with entries batched — so it only deferred delivery to the NEXT frame. That frame is the squeeze: the grid stayed sized for the old rectangle while the pane had already painted at the new one.

Fixed by delivering synchronously in the callback. _viewportRafPending is deleted, not kept: the worker proposed keeping it, but its only uses were inside the wrapper, so it would have been dead code.

The worker's escalation was correct on the diagnosis and correct to refuse the renderer-side alternative (re-adding a ResizeObserver in TerminalContent would be a racing second observer). It could not make the fix because tabs.ts belonged to the placement worker, so the coordinator made it — the right division when two tasks meet in one file.

One risk the worker did not name, which I checked before changing timing: synchronous delivery inside a ResizeObserver callback can loop if delivery resizes the observed element. It cannot here — the observer watches the pane, sized by flex layout, while delivery resizes the terminal inside it, leaving the pane's contentRect untouched. Reasoning recorded in the code.

NOT VERIFIED: the squeeze visually. jsdom cannot exercise paint timing. Observation is owed and belongs to e2e or a manual check.

title: Title bar lightens on hover
description: Hovering the 'nocx' title bar makes it visibly lighter. Reported by the user against the Wails build; not yet reproduced or diagnosed — could be a hover rule bleeding from the tab bar CSS, or a native title-bar effect. Reproduce first, then decide. Note nocx-cpp removes the separate title bar entirely (frameless, Tabby-style), which may make this moot — check that before spending effort here.
acceptance_criteria: Either the hover highlight is gone, or the bead is closed as superseded by nocx-cpp.
close_reason: Superseded by the frameless work in 2c02a46, which is the second branch of this bead's own acceptance criteria. The element that lightened was the native macOS title bar; mac.TitleBarHidden removes it entirely, so there is nothing left to highlight. No dedicated fix commit exists — checked the whole log, nothing references this bead. Confirmed in style.css: hover rules exist only on .tab, .tab-close and .tab-add; .tabbar itself has none.

title: Evaluate gremlins for Go mutation testing
description: Mutation testing measures whether tests actually assert on behaviour rather than just executing it. Candidate: github.com/go-gremlins/gremlins v0.6.0 (2025-12-05, actively maintained). Rejected alternatives: gtramontina/ooze last released 2023-02-13, zimmski/go-mutesting last commit 2021-06-10 — both stale. Constraint: this suite spawns real PTYs (transport 2.5s, session 1.8s, pty 1.5s per run) and mutation testing reruns the suite once per mutant, so it cannot live in the pre-commit hook — expose it as a separate make target run on demand. Scope the first run to internal/transport and internal/session. Note it would NOT have caught the two critical defects found in review (a never-resolving promise in untested frontend code, and a goroutine ordering race), but it would have flagged the untested session-exit path.
acceptance_criteria: A make target runs gremlins over internal/transport and internal/session; surviving mutants are triaged into beads or dismissed with a reason.

title: CI actions target Node.js 20, forced onto Node 24 by the runner
description: Run 29822238195 emitted deprecation annotations on both jobs: actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4 and actions/setup-go@v5 target Node.js 20, which GitHub has deprecated and is force-running on Node.js 24. Warnings only today; they become hard failures once GitHub drops the Node 20 shim. Bump the actions to majors that target Node 24 and confirm a run stays green.
acceptance_criteria: A CI run completes with no Node.js 20 deprecation annotations.
close_reason: Already resolved in tree: all actions in ci.yml + release.yml are @v7/@v8 (Node 24 runtime); no @v4/@v5 node20-targeting actions remain. Green-run confirmation rides with the batched end-of-epic CI verification.

title: pre-commit hook checks the worktree, not the staged snapshot
description: Known limitation of .githooks/pre-commit: it runs gofumpt/golangci-lint/go test/tsc against the working tree. With a partially staged commit (some edits staged, others not), unstaged changes can make the tree pass while the committed snapshot would fail CI. The pre-commit framework solves this by stashing unstaged changes; a hand-rolled stash is risky (can lose work if the hook is interrupted). Decide deliberately: accept and document the limitation (CI stays the authoritative gate), or implement a safe stash-and-restore.
acceptance_criteria: Either the limitation is documented in AGENTS.md as a deliberate tradeoff, or the hook validates the staged snapshot safely.

title: Missing glyphs: some TUI symbols (powerline/Nerd Font) render as '?' — ghostty-web font lacks them
description: Agent TUIs (e.g. Hermes) use special glyphs (powerline separators / Nerd Font icons) that ghostty-web's default font does not include, so they render as replacement '?'/box chars. Cosmetic, low priority. Fix later: bundle/configure a font with wide glyph coverage (a Nerd Font) or investigate ghostty-web font fallback.
close_reason: Not a font bug. The '?' glyphs were U+FFFD from UTF-8 sequences split across WebSocket frames (see the ipc.ts decode fix), not missing Nerd Font/powerline coverage. Glyph probe across all three renderers came back clean.

title: contracts/vault.resetPreview.schema.json is not prettier-formatted
description:
## Context

`prettier --check .` at the repo root fails on `contracts/vault.resetPreview.schema.json` — the `required` array is expanded one element per line where prettier wants it on one. The file has been like this since e7ea5b8; the pre-commit gate did not catch it because it checks staged files, and the file has not been staged since.

Noticed while running the full gate before 8d9408f. Unrelated to that work.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `./frontend/node_modules/.bin/prettier --check .` from the repo root.
2. It reports `[warn] contracts/vault.resetPreview.schema.json` and exits 1.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `prettier --check .` from the repo root exits 0 on a clean tree.
- Worth deciding in the same pass whether the pre-commit gate should check the whole tree rather than only staged files — a formatting drift that only a full run can see is a gate that does not hold.

title: frontend/dist/index.html is tracked but its hashed assets are gitignored
description: git tracks frontend/dist/index.html while .gitignore excludes frontend/dist/* — so the repo carries an HTML file referencing asset filenames that are not in the repo, and it churns on every npm run build. Compounding it, the negation '!frontend/dist/index.html' sits ABOVE 'frontend/dist/*' in .gitignore, and since the last matching pattern wins, the negation is overridden and only has no effect because the file is already tracked. Pre-existing, not caused by any recent change. Decide: untrack dist entirely (Wails regenerates it), or fix the pattern order and commit the assets.
acceptance_criteria: Either frontend/dist is fully untracked, or the .gitignore pattern order is corrected and the tracked set is self-consistent.
close_reason: Already resolved: frontend/dist has only the intentional .gitkeep //go:embed anchor tracked; index.html untracked; .gitignore orders 'frontend/dist/*' then '!.gitkeep' correctly. Tracked set self-consistent.
